I love this game. I've logged tons of hours into it. If games that frustrate you tend to make you stop playing because of difficulty, than this is not the game for you. However, I love the replayability and reinterpretation the particular challenge of this game provides. Finally getting your first victorious playthrough where you finally reach coronation is really satisfying. After that, it's interesting to figure out what you can do differently and learn how some of the decisions you didn't understand the first time around affect the total gameplay. The variety of effects and endings and the ways you can learn how they are all connected intrigue me time and time again. So if you like replayable, short games and something that's a bit of a challenge and mostly story-based, than you'll probably enjoy this. Bonus points if you're a Meg Turney fan, she's cosplayed the main character before.

An amazing and exciting game of Tower Defence genre! I have tried many different games of this genre, but at the moment, Warstone TD impressed me more than any other TD game. This game didn't seem to be your usual TD game, it's not just another representative of its genre, it has some uniqueness to it. And despite the fact that the genre of the game is specifically defined as Tower Defense, the sensations during the game are completely different, as if it is really trying to draw into you something more than just a simple TD game.
Perhaps a really enjoyable and interesting story plays a very important role, since it gets you involved in action from the first minutes of the game and makes you the chosen one. The in game's story is presented in the form of pleasant comics style dialoges, which I find amazing!
But perhaps the unique, in my opinion, for this genre gameplay and I mean the way the game is built, thoroughly thought out, and things you can do, when the opportunities are given to you.
Warstone TD is definitely for any kind of player, even if you aren't familiar with this kind of type of games. At the very beginning there is a tutorial that will help you get used to the controls. And even here the developer thought about the players and made the training pleasant and easy, which point deserves attention. In the course of the campaign, the player will not only have to defend an important control point by any means, reflecting waves after waves of enemies, but also to participate in the offensive part of the game, trying to win earlier than the enemy does. The player will have to build his kingdom, where each building will perform its specific function. And the more the kingdom grows, the more opportunities are revealed. The battlefield, the alignment of troops, improving unit characteristics, the distribution of upgrades after leveling, the use of various magic, artifacts - with all this player will have to get acquainted during the game.
The graphics are just astonishing, enjoyable and bright picture! The great sound quality and atmospheric musical accompaniment perfectly highlights the moment of battle. The game has achievements, the fulfillment of which only fuels your interest. For Russian-speaking players there is Russian localization!
To summarize, it can be said that this is really an impressive, worthy product, with a good implementation!

Really great Tower Defense. Has some similarities to Kingdom Rush, but is not a carbon copy. The main thing that I didn't like about Kingdom Rush is having melee blockers on the path and the game being unplayable without utilizing them efficiently. This game takes that out. It has melee "characters" (read: Towers) but it's more in the vein of Defender's Quest, where they attack like a normal tower but have a very short range.
Warstone TD has a neat persistant city that you upgrade throughout the game, buildings giving you access to: different troops on missions, upgrading the power of troops, and providing resources periodically (by levels completed, I believe, not by any sort of time passage.) You use the resources gained; iron, wood, magic, mithral, and gold; to purchase upgrades for your troops, which can be anything from a simple damage; range; or attack speed boost, to special abilities given to a certain unit.
Probably my favorite part of the additions this brings to tower defense is the Skill trees, which are huge. Some of the skills are still being implemented, but it looks like it has great potential. An interesting part of the tree is that there are skills in the "Warlord" branch that allow your units to get "ranks" during missions after a certain amount of kills, doing more damage. This, in itself, is not new to TD games, but as an inclusion in the skill tree, it can be levelled up to reduce the amount of kills required to "rank" up.
There are several spelling errors and questionable grammar, though not nearly as many as I would have expected from a secondary-language english developer.
The story and comics are well done, and at least mildly amusing, Shattering the 4th wall at times.
Fantastic game so far. Only the first few levels are currently available to play. Will try to update at a later date.

Warstone TD is a game where players must defend their realm from invading enemies.
The beasts and evil trolls attempt to pass through a defended area to reach the end of the map. You’ve got a map, an access point that needs to be defended at any cost and a horde of approaching enemies.
Each level is essentially a series of paths, with positions (warstones) where you can build your towers (summon a units upon warstones). The enemies attack in waves, and you need to stop them from reaching your base.The coins are earned upon each killing the enemy.
There are many spells (Firewall, Lightning, Meteor, Elemental summon, Poisonous cloud, Astral warriors, Transmutation etc.), different game modes (Classic TD, PvP, Co-op missions), 3 game classes (Commander, Sorcerer, Treasurer) and big skill tree for every unit.
The market is so saturated with crappy knockoffs that finding something that is simply okay is like finding treasure. Warstone TD are done with finesse relative to many other games. It feels like a finished and polished product! The game is cute, frantic and challenging. Warstone TD is very good game!

In game Warstone TD everything is done conscientiously and qualitatively.
In the role of the towers are the stones of war.
On these stones, we call on the defenders.
Each defender has a certain weapon and a set of skills.
To install a defender on the stone will need gold.
Defenders can be improved.
The possibility of improvements depends on what skills you have discovered in the Tree of Knowledge and what improvements have been made in the Laboratory building in between missions.
All of the levels in Warstone TD are so well designed.
I cannot find any faults with them at all.
The early stages of the game are a tutorial stage really.
The graphics in Warstone TD are really nice.
They are in the cartoon style that many of us really enjoy.
But they aren't so childish that they can't portray the maturity of the title.
There are some really nice special effects. Everything is perfectly animated.
I enjoyed this game.
I would strongly recommend this game to just about anyone.

Enormously frustrating game. Due to dogfight mode (DFM), enemies have a lot of health and are very hard to kill without DFM. Further, when an enemy engages you in DFM, the games breaks you off of any enemy you are pursuing, and forces you to escape the enemy's DFM (not that hard, but annoying and takes time away from playing the objective).
The flight controls are not real flight controls; stick right does not mean roll right, the game interprets that as "turn right", so it rolls you a bit but just enough to turn in the horizontal plane. I think stick forward also means "descend", rather than "pitch down", and these stick commands have caused me to crash several times (when trying to do a loop to escape a missile or something). If you do a half-loop and get upside down, you have to wait for the game to flip you back over (of course it does this right as you DFM an enemy, breaking you off), since you can't roll yourself. On top of that, the game does not remember your settings, I had to reset my control settings each time I played, which was extremely annoying.
Don't get this game, just wait for Ace Combat 7.

One of the best JRPG games ever made, now on PC.
Tales of Symphonia is considered by many as the best game in the Tales of... series. And it's very easy to see why: the story is great, the characters are VERY memorable and well developed, the combat system is amazing... there's almost nothing wrong with this game. Sure, there are some chichés here and there, some cringe-worthy dialogues... but all that is easy to forgive when the game feels so special.
For the ones that don't know, the Tales of... games are a series of Japanese RPGs with big emphasis on character development and the storyline. The stories are full of fantasy, and usually blends drama and comedy in a fantastic and natural way. The game WILL make you laugh and cry throughout the journey, and nothing feels forced.
The combat system is not turn based, like most JRPGs. Instead, you control one character directly in an action based combat kinda similar to fighting games (but more simplistic). The other characters are controlled by the AI, and this AI can be configured to work like you want it to. Also, in battles, you can open the menu at any time and give orders to the secondary characters. As long as they aren't being attacked, they will obbey your orders. It's a very good system, since it keeps the strategy of most JRPGs, while being more dynamic than turn based combat.
This version of the game is based on the PS3 version, meaning we can choose between Japanese and English voices, there are more skillsm skits, clothes, etc.
Yes, this is a great game. However, how good is the PC port?
-THE PC PORT:
The PC port had a horrible start. At release, it was not very good. The rendering resolution was locked at 720p, making the game look very pixelated, the black outlines around the characters was nowere to be found, there wwew issues saving the game, etc. I'm glad to say, however, that everything seems to be fixed now. You can use high resolutions (up to 4k), and the game WILL render at that resolution. The game has graphic options now, the black utlines are back, controls can be rebinded, etc. It may not be an amazing port, but has everything a basic PC port needs.
Keep in mind that this version is locked at 30 FPS, though. It didn't bother me THAT much, but it would be great to have 60 FPS. It's not gamebreaking, though.
Anyway. I'm recommending this game. Fact is, even though it's not the best PC port, the game itself is just amazing, and DESERVES a playthrough. And thanks to the recent patches, this is the best looing version of Symphonia ever, You can even use MSAA to make the game look amazing at any resolution you choose. ^^

This game takes place, as it says in the title, in the world of Middle-earth. The world everyone who has seen or read the Hobbit and teh Lord of the Rings knows very well. To those who want a good Middle-earth game, that captures the spirit of the books and movies, better go look somewhere else. Because even though there are a few characters in this game, that will be familiar, it really is its very own thing in terms of atmosphere and tone.
For everyone who "just" wants a good and damn fun game: Get this game!
The emphasis here lies on "fun". The real strong point of this game is the actual gameplay. The movement and the fighting system borrows a lot from Assassins Creed and other Warner Brothers games (Batman games, Mad Max).
This game just adds a sword and a dagger into the mix and merges it all together wonderfully.
The main thing xou do in this game is killing orcs. And it is simultaneously the most fun thing to do.
There is quite a variety of enemies and the addition of the "Nemesis System" adds to the variability of your enemies.
I won't go into detail about the Nemesis System, but it is a nice addition which gives the game a bit more flavor, which it lacks in other parts.
The story is the main point on the list of bad features. The characters are pretty boring and the story itself isn't really interestung either. I also don't like the way they implemented esspecially the story missions. They are placed seemingly random on the map without any real reason why you would gp exactly there in order to play the mission.
So in conclusion:
Pros:
+ insanely good gameplay (esspecially the fighting system)
+ graphics are pretty good
+ fairly interesting DLCs
+ Nemesis System
Cons:
- story
- eventually gets repetetive
- mission implementation
- nothing for hardcore Middle-earth enthusiasts
All in all a game that keeps afloat by it's absolutely amazing gameplay, with it's deficits in the story department.

Coming into this game, my expectations weren't super high. There are some features that could be better, no doubt, but for what it is, and the short time that I played it at the time of writing this review, I do recommend it.
Compared to other Civ games, it's light, but the features that are in it make it pretty fun (even though they could do with some touching up). It seems like most people don't like the game very much, but for it's price, if your a fan of Civ games and other space games as well, I'd say give it a shot. It's not the greatest by any means, but still worth a look. I'm sure with future patches, the game will get better (hopefully).
Pros:
-The ships for each affiliation (Supremacy, Harmony, Purity) look pretty good and when upgrading them, their look changes with each corresponding upgrade.
-The way you get control of different planets is pretty cool (in my opinion)
-A decent amount of leaders to choose from each with different bonuses
-The battle and movement animations look nice and fairly smooth
-Tactical battles are pretty fun, but may get boring quickly depending on who you face. (Pirates are a constant thing when it comes to the quests)
-Easy to learn and understand the mechanics.
Cons:
-The camera control is pretty awful. I get it was made for mobile as well as PC, but really? You can only move the camera with the arrow keys and it's pretty bad, especially in battles.
-Quests to control planets can get repetitive; most of the time it's just beating up pirates of some sort, though since I've only just started playing, it may change as you go along (doubtful though).
-There are no graphical options at all, and the fullscreen mode (at least for me) shows my taskbar still at the bottom of my screen. Minor, but can be annoying.
-The affiliations are cool, but I wish there was a little more variety with them. The only real difference I've noticed so far are different looking ships and a different starting bonus.
-The research "tree" is...lackluster to say the least.
That's about all for now. I'll update this review further as I play and as they patch the game in the future.
Personally, I do recommend it, but don't expect a huge amount, cause it's not Civ, but nevertheless, it's still pretty fun to play.
Thanks for reading, guys!

I've watched hours of videos on how to play this game before I bought it so don't let the hours I have in it at the moment deceive you. So far this is the best game I've played in years, Honestly my entire life I've looked for a game with such an easily customizable AI system that's still super in-depth as this one.
Don't get me wrong, however. This game is NOT easy. The controls aren't easy, the mechanics aren't easy, and even the battles aren't easy. This game is more than just a challenge for your reaction skills though. This game is a challenge for your brain. Coming up with new and innovative ways to use the mechanics to make amazing creations for either looks or potency is what is, has, and will always be what separates this game from the others. This game is Minecraft on steroids. If you enjoy being able to build legos with computers that you can program to do pretty much whatever you want, then this game is for you. I would highly recommend even though there is one glaring issue I will address down below.
I'll cut the developer some slack and let any bugs slide for now since it is after all an alpha. The one thing I do have slight issue with however is the framerate. My pc is more than capable of running most games and in smaller engagements I lose slim to no fps. However in the larger battles and even the benchmark it goes and stays around 10-12 fps on the lowest settings. I sincerely hope the dev will have some sort of breakthrough in the code to get more performance out of the larger battles because that's the only thorn in the side of this game right now.
Other than that, I would recommend this to only the more intelligent of my friends. Not to insult anyone's intelligence but unless you're smarter than the average gamer, this game will get on your nerves quickly with all of the mechanics it has available. It can easily overwhelm a newbie or a more casual gamer so take caution, this game is not for the faint of mind.

I learned about failsafes, weapon control, AI cards, and that the AI would rather back up towards a target than complete a turn to use forward propulsion in an approach vector.
Day 5: Dear Diary, today I applied for a Doctorate in Mechanical Engineering with MIT despite only having 30 credit hours. I sent footage of From the Depths along with my application. Today one of my shells bounced against an enemies armor, came back, entered through a hole I keep in the deck to get to the engine, and hit my ammunition cache causing the entire belly of the ship to blow out. AdVenture Communist puts you as a communist who has to grow potatoes, magically produce land, mine rock, create bullets and pills. You can buy robots to help you, but robots are also resources.
And I must say, I was starting to get hooked onto this game. This is a major step-up from AdVenture Capitalist, and this is only in early access!
You just don't sit their, clicking on random items and waiting for products to give you money, actually, what you generate is your money. You grow potatoes and generate land to be able to get farmers, grow more potatoes, generate more land and have get rid of 5 farmers to get workers etc. And the more times you click the button, the more you'll get when you upgrade. The more robots you buy, the more items they get.
There is now also an option to turn down the Master Sound, Music Sound and SFX Sound, which is amazing for me since I couldn't hear myself when I recorded AdVenture Capitalist.
You also don't need to pay to progress quickly. I made $400,000+ in less than 20 minutes, and you could probably make more!
I hope in the future, achievements and cards are added.
I must admit, when I found out this game existed, I had low standards about Hyper Hippo Games, but playing this raised my standards. I hope the next game you release is better.
But I still don't feel like I'm getting entertained from this. This is a good time-waster game, but I have 63 other games I could play (at the time of writing this review) and I don't see this making my favourites list.
Overall, this is a massive step-up from AdVenture Capitalist, but I want more gameplay. Like dragging a rake along dirt to pick up potatoes instead of just clicking a button. Or moving my mouse around clouds to find land. Or clicking stone to pick it up. Or having to drag materials onto a conveyor belt to make bullets. Or having to put pill packs into a box to get medicine. I'm giving you some ideas here.
If you were one of the people who somehow loooved AdVenture Capitalist, I feel like trying out this game is a necessity for you.

the very moment i saw the game i knew the style of graphics - this must be the GUARDS - the game i've played and reviewed. it appeared not the Guards, but the new game from a same developer - Warstone tower defense.
I love playing tower defence games, played them a lot and this one feels to be the best tower defence game i've ever played, maaaaybe with the only exception of Graveyard - the game i've played long ago on a tablet. Anyway, now these two share the first place in a top chart of all tower defense games that i've ever played. But lets get to the detail.
First, graphics, as i've already said i've knew it from the very first sight, and that was truth - design is - i'm not afraid to say - overwhelming. I just adore how everything is done - yes, maybe there some design know-hows that share both games Guards and Warstone, but that's not just ok, that's perfect when the best from Guards got a new life. Anyway - its neither too much, nor too little, great balance between what is important and what is not, great UI and great UX
Second - gameplay. Game's very addictive, greatly balanced, if you are losing lives you are definitely doing something wrong - in towerdefence games you should be very tight in resources, very exact and quick in tower building (in these game its a hero placing) than the game is interesting. If its either too hard or too easy player might lose interest in both cases. So, i will repeat, this one is great, because its balanced.
and a third thing i was just not expecting to see: most of towerdefense games are just pure tower defense levels that start one after another, yes, you might get upgrades in between, but usually you don't leave the level choice interface for it. This one has a big superstructure built upon some "general" towerdefense - a whole another strategy world, where you talk to a magician responsible for different spells, build and upgrade whole little kingdom - like a base in any real strategy game your forces are leaving and returning to!
though the game is "early access" the only problem i had from time to time was "losing connection to server" or something similar - game itself behaved perfectly.
as a conclusion - there are not so many games that make me to find a developer and visit developers website. Usually these games are made by some moster big studios like Bethesda or Paradox but this small indie game, second, published in steam by a small studio is definitely one of them.

Setting up a camp- deciding what buildings to develop (med, ammo, sniper nests etc). Talking to people that are depressed/have issues helps more than you realise.If you send someone on a mission to collect resources they will physically go across the map and attempt to collect and return. You must kit them out well if you dont want them to die. If they die, any resources they collected will drop at the place of death. Little details like this make this game special. LOADS of weapons/ammo types/items. Shooting is perfect, the lighting is beautful. Its a reminder of why we play games and where the medium is going. The start of this game does not do it justice.
Keep on playing people!

I think it is time for a review. 250 hours in, I have a lot of heart for this game.
Starbound is very in depth, with both characters and universe. Eventually, things have become repetative as I feel like I have seen and done everything, but that is certainly to be expected after 250 hours. I have deep emotional attachments to this game, and the character custimization is seemingly endless. Another very well done game by chucklefish. The multiplayer factor works very smoothly, and is more fun to play with friends that you have dragged in to play it with you. The soundtrack is beautiful, and adds a lot of polish to different enviornments. There is so much depth and attention to story and lore that leaves a lot to be found and fuels art and fanstories to be made. The replayability is almost encouraged, as there is so much to discover and new characters are so much fun to make.
On a negative note, sometimes parkour can be a bit tedious, since the physics are a little slippery. Sometimes planets can be a little repatative, yet I am still coming across things that I have never seen before. The game itself has a very good progression that leads you to explore the vastness of it, but after the main missions are done things are left up to your own motivation. I would like to see more missions from the characters that join the ark. On a functional note, the game one day crashed after I had done nothing differently, and has since crashed occasionally without reason. I have had to install a few mods and tweak controls to get it working again.
Still, for only $15?!?! This game is totally amazing and I have recommended it to many of my friends who have since enjoyed it. I listen to the soundtrack in my free time (which is another good price deal as well) and come back to this game often. Very well done, and heavily recommended.

How do you calculate cynism, misanthrophy and a "good" portion of bad taste into a review?
Hard to say, but I can say, the mixture does work, this game - as evil as it might seem, and as dated as it is, has a lot of merits.
First and foremost it is very linear in gameplay, everybody knows exactly what is going on. And yes, it's the term "going postal" that is giving this game it's title. The USPS Incidents in the mid 80s shocked the public, the term "Workplace Rage" was also stamped out in that time.
This game was over a long time an inside tip. Sometimes it was hard to even get this game, in some countries it was even on an index. This of course led to the popularity that the game still holds.
Of course, this game isn't exactly rocket science, it's a simple isometric shooter, with the only objective to shoot enough antagonists, to open up the next area. Do your qouta and all is well. Your own weapons can hurt you too, so be carefull if you use rocketlaunchers, grenades, molotov cocktails - they can harm you too.
Humor, real black humor of course, is a rarity in this game. There are some moments, when the developers let it shine, but they are quite real in this game. It's sinister on purpose, but that is exactly what is creating this "hidden" charm. Even though it's not a rich game at all. But for a game that was developed in 1997 it is an ok game, and there were back at that time already games that were even far more gory than Postal.
And no, the programmers didn't glorify killing sprees, they wrote a programm about a person who went on one, and if you think why someone would do such a thing, you are half on your way to your own answer. Why would anybody play Rambo? Or The Hobbit? Or even try to be an ancient god (Populous, Black & White)? Or try to be a starship captain?
Can I recomend the game? Yes. Is it the best game I ever had? Definitly not, but it also isn't among the worst for that matter. The graphics are dated, some people might get problems with the isometric view, others might be disgusted by the "story" of the game, or the gore. The Sound might annoy some people too. But still it is a playable and easy game. And it's worth the 5 €.

In all of an hour and a misguided summer sale purchase... I've been scarred. This... this isn't an Ace Combat game. The title makes you want to believe otherwise, but... the bad reviews? They're earned. If you're like me, coming into this from AC5 expecting a compelling story and aggressive, edge of your seat fights amid swarms of enemy fighters looking to gun you down...
...Prepare for disappointment.
The name of the game is initiate Dogfight Mode and let the game fly for you as you effortlessly push buttons as RNG decides if your missiles hit or if the enemy dodges your gunfire.
Not to mention the game itself strays from air combat and dogfights to put you in the seat of interactive cutscenes- or as they want to call them, door/AC-130 gunner positions.
The game is, from what I can tell, an interactive movie and little else. The raw air maneuvers are clunky and at times unintuitive, especially when using Dogfight Mode (which they make almost essential to defeat enemy Aces)
The killcams are pretty, I like being able to chip off shards of the enemy fighters... but that's about where the charm of this game ends for me.
Let's hope they don't make the same mistakes in AC7.

Shadow of Mordor is an enjoyable experience. Besides the nemesis system that is new to this instalment you probably have seen gameplay like this already, that gameplay being from the Batman Arkham series, but its not a weakness by any means, the combat is still very engaging and once you unlock all of your talents and legendary weapons you can survive most of what the game throws at you, my only complain would be that near the endgame it gets a bit harder to find those large groups of orcs again.
The stealth is very straightforward, in fact, its rather simple, you just press the stealth button and most orcs won't discover you even if they see you directly as long as you have some distance between him and you and wait for his attention bar to fade, you definitively won't have problems completing the stealth kill bonuses some missions give you, its pretty barebones but it works when you take into consideration the amount of orcs the game throws at you if an alarm is raised, especially if you are still starting the game, be aware though, the list of orc captains that can be killed with stealth is small, so in most missions you will probably end up fighting directly anyway.
The music of the game is great, I have no complains about it, but you will probably hear it a lot to the point of recognizing the songs if you go play the completionist route. It's not the heroic Lord of The Rings trilogy orchestra but tribal and aggressive, you're in Mordor after all, hearing the orc chants, especially when a warchief arrives to the scene never gets old.
The story in the game is nothing special but does its job, some of the characters don't get much screentime but the ones that do are likeable, its worth it just for the cutscenes with Celebrimbor's past alone. You get to visit 2 zones from Mordor and they are very well done.
The duration of the game is kind of complicated to describe, all the content is there for you to play but the story missions are not very long, in fact there's just 20 main story missions so it can be finished quickly. The real meat of the game lies in the side content you can do, you can collect ancient artifacts scattered around Mordor, rescue all the slaves, complete all the challenges with combat, stealth and archery in order to get the legendary version of those weapons and the most important thing of all, you can brand all the orcs and give them positions of power with the nemesis system. The good news is that the game of the year edition is the version you will be buying so you get 2 DLCs with extra content, one takes place in the second zone of the game with Talion and the other one lets you play with Celebrimbor in the first zone of the game, he plays quite differently from Talion so at that point it will feel like a breath of fresh air.
Just be aware, as fun as the gameplay is, most of the things you'll be doing will probably feel repetitive at the end, so you might get burned out, I'd recommend not finishing both dlcs in one sitting.
One more thing I'd like to point out, the combat is fun but there will be a few parts in the game where you have to deal with quick time events, denying a finishing blow, executing a warchief or dealing with a story mode boss. The Nemesis system is not as fleshed out as in Shadow of War but it beats having to grind the final portion of the game to avoid the lootboxes.

If you're looking at this, I have to assume you've played this game before, so I wil be brief in my review of the actual game:
It's the Tales of Symphonia you loved and remembered. So far I can't see a single thing changed (which, apparently, is a bad thing for some folks, but the rest of us are just happy to get a game we loved back in highschool).
If you have not played ToS before, it's a very vibrantly-colored, exciting game with an emotionally-charged story. The dialogue is hammy, but it's endearing and, honestly, if it wasn't hammy the whole game might take itself too seriously.
The port isn't nearly as bad as folks are making it out to be. There were some hiccups in the beginning with customize/save screen taking a bit of time to come up, but that has been patched out. Graphics options being "non-existent" is a bit confusing to me, as it's a port of a 12-13 year old game: what were you looking for, exactly? You can choose between fullscreen or windowed, and it supports up to 1920x1080.
Controller support is excellent. It's almost like this game was made with an Xbox controller in mind.
I have had exactly zero crashes and the slow-loading menu issue was patched out by the second time I started it up. It's a decent port of an excellent game. Of note, apparently certainly anti-virus programs will be set off by this game? I don't have the issue, so.. I can't comment on it?

I played and finished Adventure Capitalist and now I spent around 10 hours clicking in Adventure Communist. So far Communist looks like better game, or should I say it has potential to be better game.
In communist you have 5 tabs dedicated to production of 5 different resources. The point of the game is to farm the 6th resource which is the one everyone is crying about because you can buy it with micro transactions, and that is the only thing you can buy. So if you ask me spending money on game is pointless and it would be the same as paying to see the ending in other games.
When comparing Communist and Capitalist there are few differences. While in capitalist you just buy everything and go afk until you get enough money for more stuff or enough angels to reset, in communist first thing you will notice is that you are rewarded for clicking... on daily base. This means that there are daily bonuses which you can get while clicking, but the ammount of resources you get from clicks become insignificant really fast. 2nd notable thing is that reset in communist is limited only to 1 tab or I should say that each tab is reseted individually, and with resets you start the production of 6th resource.
Why is the 6th resource important? You buy all the upgrades with it, upgrades increase production of other 5 resources which enable you to get the 6th resource faster. The end.
But there are few issues with the game atm. There are bugs (the one I notice the most is being able to buy more stuff even though you dont have enough resources to actually get it. example: you have enough resources to buy 100 communes, but from time to time when you switch between tabs the ammount of communes you can actually buy jumps to 1000 even though you still have enough resources for 100).
The game doesn't look as if it is going to be long. I played it for 3 days and I get around 70 scientist (6th resource) every 4 hours and to put that in perspective the most expensive upgrade is 10k.
There are no events.
Tl;dr More interesting than capitalist, and don't listen to people who are crying about micro transactions because they obviously haven't played the game at all.

A battle was raged, the combatants vying for control of the "Holy Grail." With this power, they could make any wish come true, reshaping the very face of reality to make it so. The war has ended, the victor sits upon his throne with his servant, and lover, by his side. Oh, also the war took place on the moon, everyone was digitally constructed out of "spiritons," and your servant/lover is the mind of Nero Claudius, reborn as a busty blonde. So, you know, a run of the mill story.
This was my first experience with the Fate series, so learning all of these details was something of a shock, though not an unpleasant one. Say what you will about anime and Japanese games, but there's no doubt that they do not lack for creativity. While this was my first time handling the series, this was the series' first time within the action genre, taking the Musou sub-type for its inaugural outing. Before Fate/Extella, the series existed as visual novels and RPGs. This entry also marks the first time that the player would be able to take direct control of the Servants (the embodiments of historical and mythological figures). This title was developed by Marvelous Inc., makers of the Story of Seasons and Senran Kagura games, two series that couldn't be more different. If you're wondering if the "bouncing physics" of Senran Kagura games make it over to Fate/Extella, they do.
No one can say the premise of this game isn't unique. Following the Holy Grail War, you were all set to settle down with your busty general when a terrible evil befell you. The result left you scattered into three pieces, each one ending up with a different Servant. The story is told from several different perspectives from several different characters. At first I thought this was a Rashomon style of story, but the events in the different campaigns differ, so these are more like alternate time lines.
While the story is certainly unique, the writing of the dialogue and the characters is exhausting and tropey. Any anime fan will instantly recognize characters simply by the way they stand and the first words the say. The romantic dialogue between Master and Servant is like something out of a high schooler's fanfiction. This is my first go in this series, so I don't know if this is par for the course, but I have heard from others (who have played the other games and watched the animes) that they enjoyed the story in this one. If nothing else, if you're only here for the Musou, you can skip the scenes with two button presses.
The game falls into the Musou sub-genre, joining the likes of Dynasty Warriors and Hyrule Warriors. If you're still not sure what this means, what you'll be doing is running around a battlefield going up against hundreds of enemies at once, totalling up thousands of corpses by the end. You are a one-man army, carving large swathes of destruction with easily executed combo moves and special attacks. Your main goal will be to take back sectors of the map, eventually getting enough ground to drive out the Boss and face them in combat.
Musou games are great for unwinding and relaxing. There's not much though required in these games, assuming you play on Normal or Easy. Hard and Very Hard may require more careful planning, but any challenge can usually be overcome by leveling yourself beyond the recommended amount. Imagine playing Bayonetta or Devil May Cry, except against a half dozen enemies you face hundreds, and instead of a long combo list of varying buttons you have a shorter one with all moves starting with Light Attack and ending with a Heavy Attack.
Make no mistake, I love these kinds of games, and any fan of Musou games will likely enjoy playing through this one as well. Its only hiderance, beyond the limitations of the genre, is a sluggish camera that gets pushed up against walls with you and the inability to lock-on to enemies besides Servants. I don't mean the small enemies, locking onto them would be insane. Rather, it would have been nice to be able to lock onto the sub-bosses you have to defeat to take a sector back.
PROS
+ Musou-style hack 'n' slash is relaxing and fun.
+ Large cast of diverse characters (all of which are playable!)
+ 20+ hour campaign and even more for the side content.
+ Waifus based on historical monsters, because why not.
CONS
- Frustrating camera and limited lock-on.
-Story hampered by exhausting and poorly written dialogue.

Surprisingly very fun arcade-y game.
I'm always skeptical when in comes to pseudo-retro games, especially ones with lo-fi graphics, but obviously this is among the good ones. Basically, you pilot a plane, avoiding bullets & missiles while shooting down your many adversaries. As you play & achieve things, you are rewarded with new plane parts interchangeable in-between runs (runs are basically infinite and can only be renewed when you die). These parts are divided into weaponry, body & thruster.
However, newer parts are not necessarily superior. All parts comes with their own pluses & minuses, based on the special property it carries (like a body made of a nuclear warhead, yeah, go figure). So it depends on your combination & how you play them.
Equipping certain parts also means you are only allowed to unlock certain achievements. However, this can also be used to your advantage. For example, one of the achievement missions  for the basic machine gun would be to take down a battleship. This is to say, a rather impossible task. However, if you equip your plane with the nuclear warhead body while also equpping the machine gun, you can simply run into the ship to kill it, you, and everything else on the screen and there you have it. One battleship down while 'using' the machine gun.
The game doesn't have any story, but it doesn't need one anyways. The setting is enough to give you the idea that it's a war, and you are just one among the many disposable soldiers.
That said, due to the nature of the game it probably has low lasting appeal. However, due to its simplicity (doesn't necessarily mean it's easy though, far from it) it's also an easy pick up and play for when you just want to play a game but isn't in the mood to think much, but still wants more or less a challenge. If you don't have a game like that in your library yet, you might want to get this.

(I also owned this Xbox360 originally) As an Ace Combat fan since AC 4 on PS2, this one is the worse in the series. So why am I recommending it? Well, it is still a fun game, when you get past the idea that this is not a true AC game. DFM (Dog Fight Mode) ruins the gameplay, it's a gimmick introduced to the game to help casual players to stay on enemies tails and makes the game look more cinematic... it kind of introduces cool cutscenes mixed with gameplay which are half the time scripted pursuits... which means you will shoot an enemy a ton, but they will not die until the game decides it's time for the ennemy to die. Also some enemies cannot be taken down unless you use this annoying feature. This is at it's worse at the last dog fight in the game where you keep pursuing this one ennemy and shoot him like 60 times but he keeps on kicking. Bosses are usually tougher in every Ace Combat games, but it breaks the immersion when you shoot the ennemy to hell, and he seems to heal almost as soon as you shot him, only to go down when the game script says "okay, we are in the location we want you to be so now the enemy can die"... it's a bullcarp frustrating fight. Speaking of healing... this game is clearly aimed at the casual crowd, as your plane heals itself as if it was freaking Call of Doody. Actually Ace Combat Horizon is what I consider the call of Doody of ace combat games. I still had my share of fun, but this campaign is super short compared to other games in the franchise. I played a tiny bit of the multiplayer On Xbox 360, and was frustrated to see they carried that DFM feature into multiplayer, I cannot wait to play AC 7 where I am sure they are removing this feature to play with players with actual dog fighting skills. In conclusion, a very short 4-6 hour campaign which still have some fun value, the multiplayer is pretty much dead, and a little something to pick up at a sale for 5$ if you feel bored or want to scratch that flyer's itch... though it will be a very light scratch.

Middle-earth: Shadow of Mordor is an excellent game set within Tolkien's Middle-earth, although taking a few liberties with canon in order to make the story and gameplay more engaging and fun, and it does an excellent work at it.
The story takes place somewhere between the events of The Hobbit and the Lord of the Rings trilogy. In it, you play as Talion, a ranger of the Black Gate who was killed when the gate was sieged by the Black Hand of Sauron, and later binded to the spirit of Celebrimbor, forger of the Rings of Power. Like I said, the story takes some liberties with canon, but it ends up being excellent, as you fight through Mordor in order to stop, or at the very least delay, Sauron's return.
The gameplay is incredibly good. Very similar to the gameplay of the Batman: Arkham games, the combat feels very fluid with all the movement freedom you get, as well as the extra combo finishers you unlock as you progress. The stealth is also very good, allowing you to distract enemies from the shadows or attract them to your location in order to eliminate them one by one, and you also get a bow, which, besides being an excellent long range weapon, it ends up becoming a great mobility tool. However, what makes this game shine is the Nemesis system, in which orcs who kill you get stronger, and you can also gain intel on them in order to know their strenghts, weaknesses, and fears. When killing Captains or Warchiefs, you also get special runes for each of your weapons, granting you bonuses.
I can't say much for the soundtrack; it's not that it's bad, it's rather good actually, but there isn't something that really stands out. Some pretty good warlike tunes play whenever you start fighting large amounts of orcs, and whenever a Warchief shows up, a chorus shouts his name along with the music. The voice acting is pretty good, especially when it comes to the orc Captains and Warchiefs, who get different voice lines according to their titles, as well as past encounters with the player. If you killed them but they return (or viceversa) they'll even comment on that.
Well, I think that's enough for this review. A pretty solid game set in Middle-earth, with some good combat systems, and lots of gameplay possibilities. I recommend it.

I bought this game during the steam sales, thinking it was a nice little 3-4€ bargain that I would play for a few days.
Boy was I wrong.
From my first awful wooden ship with barely enough engine power to move forward, to enormous death juggernauts of doom I build now, I have fun every time.
I sometimes just think of a clever little idea during the day, load the game really quickly to try it out, usually fail miserably, and have a good laugh doing it.
The game is update regularily, the only time I've seen it crash was that time I spawned two ships that could be Warhammer 40K canon and made them duke it out, and that's only because my potato of a computer just couldn't keep up with the carnage.
Beginners pick up the game quite fast, and all the little, harder to master things are details, so don't hinder new players from enjoy the game, and you learn constantly from your machines and the pre-built selection of ships.
As for the avid coders? You're in luck! The game allows you to tweak integrated AI functions (like navigation). A little search through the forums and I saw people making scripts for hovercrafts, spaceships and even smart flares to counter missiles more effectively.
TL;DR This game is fun, addictive and you can build so many, many things. Yes, even a giant phallus that shoots out explosive shells. I know you're going to do it, so why lie?

I am absolutely in love with this game! It seems to have no external purchases necessary, you can make gold super simple!
Gold helps you buy new themes as backdrops (and some of them even change the way the stars look!). Gold drops down randomly, and it's a fun challenge to try to catch gold without letting stars "die" by hitting the ground.
The mechanics are very simple: you move the basket on the ground with whichever keys you want, and you activate some special abilities that you can purchase via that gold with Shift or Y. You're trying to catch stars, avoid ice chunks, and catch power-ups while avoiding power-downs. There's a neat little wind mechanic that I've found useful (and good to keep an eye on).
There is music, some of which is original some of which isn't, but it all fits really nicely into the themes.
It is a delightful game. Definitely an Indie title, as it doesn't come with the bells and whistles of others. Even that, though, is something to love about it. It's simple, relaxing, and very enchanting! Highly recommend this to anyone!
To the devs - you've done an amazing job. I'll keep an eye out on your other titles!

I know I am quite a few years late to this game... but the flight simulator market has never been very good on consoles... thank goodness this game got ported to PC.
Not a fan of the series, though I have played quite a few of these over the last few decades, none of them have been very good.  If you like lining up little red squares, and triangles, and then pressing a button, then maybe this game is perfect for you.  I for one found this getting old during the intro mission.
I switched up the controls to be much more complex, and still it fails to reach any sort of flight simulation, and still maintains that Arcade feel, but not of dogfighting, but rather a puzzle game, matching on screen inputs.
This is closer to an airborne guitar hero, than it is to any sort of combat game.
Gun sounds... actually ALL the sound in this game is so weak, that you feel as if you are farting the other planes out of the sky.
Helicopter missions as a gunner, are campy, at the very most, and provide no substance to the game, but repeat the farting at nearly invisible targets, while having your view almost completely obscured.
Not fun.
Not remotely.
I consider myself a fan of flight combat, and this simply falls short on all fronts.

I'll be blunt.  I expected better.  The art style in the cutscenes is gold.  The character designs on paper are gold.  The concept is gold.  The gameplay and overall game feel and flow?  It's a piece of charred, rusted copper.  This is one of the stiffest, intuitive, and most frustrating brawlers I have ever played.
Movement is either super speed or speed force.  Don't get me wrong I like fast movement, but your range of movement is far too limited for it.  You are confined to one screen and must fend off wave after wave of enemies.  On the surface, that's fine.  However, hitting enemies isn't nearly as responsive, tight, or fun as it should be.  You have an uppercut with zero range and that's your best standard move.  The rest are a punch and dive kick(which is useless).  Enemies with more than one hitpoint stop you in place when you hit them, but due to limited range of movement the other enemies are encroaching(or diving) towards you.  Play this for the waves and you'll see what I mean.
I wanted to like this game, but I can't recommend it.  I found out about it from a game called Indivisible.  The female brawler is going to be in that game and I figured I would support that developer by buying this game.  I don't regret doing so, but I'm sure not happy about this purchase.
One more thing: I had to opt into a beta because the developer added Windows 10 support which basically made it so you couldn't even start the game anymore.  Any attempt to switch back over to normal version causes the same crash.  This game needed a lot more support and patches than it ended up getting.

This is a good game. If you've arrived at this review to see if the game is worth buying, and you have no experience with the Souls Series, then sit down and let me dispel a few myths, dispense some advice, and not spout "Git Gud" ♥♥♥♥♥♥ry at you.
Dark Souls is not hard. Hard games don't have infinite lives. Dark Souls is a fair game, and will punish you for making the same mistakes over and over.
Dying is natural. If you die, shrug, recover your souls, and carry on. Don't treat death in this game like in other games. You're expected to die in Dark Souls, its part of the game.
Do not go to the Catacombs or New Londo at the start. You will die die die die die for nothing. Go to the undead burg. Where's the Burg? When you get to Firelink Shrine, the Undead Burg is the only place you can go that goes up in elevation. Look up a map.
Use the Wiki if you get lost.
Dark Souls is a game that grows on you. At a certain point in that growth, things will become clear as to why people get addicted to this game.
And now the last bit of advice: Its perfectly fine to not like Dark Souls, Its not for everyone. My first experience with the game resulted in me getting rid of it because I just didn't have the time to learn it.

First things first. LUFTRAUSERS is a portmanteau of the German noun "Luft", meaning air, and the Dutch "cant" verb "rausen", meaning a lot of different things involving reckless or loud behaviour.
And indeed, the name is already half of the game. Without much of a warning pseudo-imperial-germanyish Dieselpunkland finds itself under attack by all kinds of flying and seafaring vessels. Enter the customisable Rauser of your chosing and deal death to those vile unknown aggressors! The battlefield loops without end and with every enemy you destroy the difficulty and number of baddies increases as you navigate your fragile little plane through an endless stream of bullets.
This game does 2 things really well.
First of all, the music (I think I always write something positive about music in my reviews...). There is only one track of music that you hear while playing. It starts off with marching feet as an underlying beat and slowly works its way up to a heroic climax. The instruments change depending on the parts you've used on your Rauser, which is a really neat and well executed idea! It is a great feeling if you survive long enough to hear the triumphant climax part of the track.
The second fantastic thing about the game is the sense of flying and speed you experience. Even tough its a 2D game, you really get a feeling of flying at break-neck speeds through the sepia coloured clouds. The controlls are just great. Stalling in mid-air, suddenly boosting away from danger, making bombing runs, it all just works like a charm. Its one of those games where you only have yourself to blame if you mess up.

Short Verison:
Starbound is a great game with beautiful terraria-esque graphics, a 2D world, and a great modding community. It recently added the long awaited "mechs-with-actual-use" and space-encounters, which to be honest, could use a bit more variation. It features a near-infinite proceduraly-generated universe that is per-filesystem, meaning all your characters play in that one universe. Nevertheless; Starbound is an amazing game, and if you like games that include space-travel, great humor, and loads of lore, Starbound is your game!
Long Version:
Ohh... where to start? Well, I guess I'll start with the world size. Unlike Minecraft or Terraria, you aren't limited to one world. In fact, Starbound has near-limitless worlds in a procedurally-generated universe that all your players play on. I've managed to start on oner world, begin another character because I missed one of the easter-eggs in the story-intro-thingy, began looking for a place to live, then stumbled across my old dwelling. Now, that's not to say the world is small, in fact I think (don't quote me on this) you can go out to the 64-bit limit on each coordinate. So, in no way is the world small. I just got incredibly lucky. The humor in Starbound's story is bountiful, the lore behind the game's setting is about as deep as you can go in such a shot-lived (yet exciting) story, and the replayability is augmented tenfold by not only the world-size, randomly-generated weapons, and rarer "special" weapons, bosses, etc etc... but also the bounty of mods on the Steam Workshop (as well as the very few on the Chucklefish forums that have yet to move over.) The story, as I said is exciting, but could use less "find and scan things for me, human/plant/monkey/fish/robot/gas person!" The main bosses of the game are challenging enough to pose a threat ill-prepared, but easy enough once you figure out their pattern, and have enough supplies/armor. On modding the game; it's easy enough to get into modding, whether you are just modifying textures, adding whole new items, or even creating whole new maps, dungeons, features, etc etc. Chucklefish gives modders a lot of leeway. Al-la the Frakin' Universe mod.
TL;DR: Starbound is an awesome game, get it if you like sandbox 2D space games!

A fun, modern-day take on a Golden Axe like melee game, with Lord of the Rings lore.
In all reality its a reskinning of the modern Batman games, with elements of Assassins Creed and Far Cry thrown in.
The melee combat is straight out of Batman, including how the camera works and how difficulty works (unselectable).
The map and missions have a Batman meets Far Cry feel to them.
The stealth feels like Assassins creed with many of the same finishing moves.
If you enjoy the mechanics and melee/archery combat then you can easily get 20-40+ hours out of it for Story and DLC, if not more.  The story is fairly contrived and although there is some great artwork, the cutscenes are mostly skippable.
Most of the joy in this one comes from the sophisticated, yet silly AI as they react to the chaos unleashed from wandering caragoers, explosive barrels, campfires, and you.  The personality of the AI is deep and whimsical, often catching modern takes on our own societal problem in the discussions overheard from the Uruks.
Technically I found the game to run great on Ultra, even on my Q9650/7990, a very outdated machine; running 1920x1200 ultra at a benchmark of 30fps->62fps (60 fps cap).
Recommend the GOTY edition when its on sale, I got mine for $5.

In my opinion the story and characters aren't well fleshed out at all, too many fleeting appearances to build up any sort of feelings on the NPC characters outwith your base and the story moves quickly to a conclusion but somehow manages to miss a trick in terms of storytelling, number of missions and variety of scenarios given the scope that the developers had to work with in a post apocalypse zombie infested setting.
Where the game sets itself apart however is in creating a persistent world. Play the game for a few hours and come back a week later to find that queued construction works have been completed, survivors have scavaged supplies from adjoining buildings, a band of neighbouring survivors have been wiped out, in your absence zombie hordes are encroaching onto your base, a survivor from your base camp has went missing and worst case scenario if morale of a survivor gets especially low a survivor may kill themself in your absence.
It's a nice touch which elevates generic gameplay mechanics, over saturated zombie themes and cliched characters into a dynamic singleplayer experience.

Well, I certainly love the second Postal game, and the third one might as well be a guilty pleasure. The first one? Well...
The first Postal, released in '97, has not aged well, in it's original release. Which is sad, because it's almost good.
First off, the actual content in the game is not the reason I think this game is bad. Even if the content was off putting (It's not for me, because you can beat the game without killing a single non-hostile cpu), the Postal games really have a blurry continuity, so weither anything in the games outside of P2 is canon is up for debate. Enough stalling, let's get to my review.

Graphically, this game is interesting. The contrast between hand-drawn enviorments and 3D models is certainly a unique style, I like it. It's a little primitive with the 3D models, but I've seen worse.
Sound design was not too kind to Postal. The effects need to be manually balanced out, some stuff is too loud, but YMMV. The droning music tracks (mainly in menus) actually work well for the games concept though.
The real problem, which is a huge one, is the controls. Yeah, you can adjust them through various means, but the fact is, I shouldn't have to. Aiming is a complete chore, and so is running through tight passages. They take time to get used to, but even then, the control is pretty terrible. It's killed all enjoyment the game has for alot of people.
Lastly, I wanna briefly mention the actual concept of the game. On one hand, it's a needlessly violent (implied really, the action on screen is pretty tame by today's standards) isometric shooter. On the other hand, it's an interesting isometric shooter with arcade-y gameplay. Either way, it was RWS's first game, and it shows. It doesn't hold up very well today. I'm glad it exists though, because it paved the way for a PC masterpiece, and a TPS that's fun despite its many bugs.
Overall, I wouldn't recommend Postal 1, but it might be worth checking out on sale for those who are curious enough. Seriously though, the controls are♥♥♥♥♥
What I do recommend, however, is the upcoming remake Postal: Redux. It fixes the controls and updates the graphics, but otherwise is the same game. I'll review it when it's released.
Now, that's my review of it's orignal release. However, the Steam version has benefited greatly from RWS patching the game up. The controls have been alterned, no longer confining to tank-controls. Instead, it controls as a top down shooter should control. Another change related to controls is proper support for controllers. I plugged my Xbox controller in and everything was already pre-configured, and comfortable to boot. Strangely, fire wasn't assigned to any button, but it was a quick fix. With these control fixes, (plus a crosshair for easier aiming) the game plays alot better and now, I'd consider it an underrated classic alongside it's amazing sequal.

Long Live the Queen uses an engine for Visual Novels, looks like Princess Maker, but plays like a roguelike.
Basic summary of the plot and gameplay: Due to her mother's sudden death, Elodie needs to survive 40 weeks before she turns 15 and is crowned Queen proper. You manage her class schedules which will increase her skills in different areas, but you must also keep track of her mood which can affect how easily she learns certain skills. These skills will become vital as they are frequently checked in events throughout the game. Failing these tests can have consequences that range from not gaining certain dialogue options to instant death.
That's the gist of it, but as you play you realize the events of the game look far more complex than it seems. A single decision can have implications several weeks down the line, sometimes interacting with several other factors that railroad you to your death. Adding to the complexity is that sometimes the game checks for skills that didn't seem superficially necessary to an event. And sometimes these checks are STEEP to the point where you'd pretty much need to have been planning to go for them from the start.
Then again, you can save and load at nearly any point in the game. Hope you've been taking notes or have a good memory. Would recommend that you only begin using a guide after the first 5 or so deaths or if you're hunting odd achievements.
There is often more than one way to skin a cat - for example, you could negotiate a compromise with an invading army to back away, or utilize an alliance to intimidate them into doing so. You're not entirely hosed for neglecting a certain skill set, but you'd better make sure whatever you've invested in is appropriately polished. And because you never have enough time to max everything out, there's a constant possibility of what happens if you resolve certain conflicts in different ways, and the challenge of managing your skills and mood such that they're up to standard when the time comes. A singe complete playthrough takes about 2 hours to accomplish, but be assured you'll spend even more time exploring other events the game has to offer.

I've played Ace Combat 2 and Ace Combat 3: Electrosphere on PS1 and one thing is sure: I loved both of them (even though I played the European version of AC03). Yes both had some flaws but generally I think they're great games and I believe most players can agree with me. After replaying AC03 I just thought why not to play the other AC games. I had PS2 but I didn't find any Ace Combat games from local game stores so I thought why not try searching Ace Combet for PC. After a while I found it: Ace Combhat: Assault Horizon. And boy it was different. I really have mixed reactions of it. In this review I'm only talking about the single player campaing since I haven't tried mutliplayer yet and probably not going to.
First of all let's talk about one of the major aspect of the game: Dog Fighting Mode (or just DFM). I kid you not, when I first started playing the game and got the first DFM, I quitted and didn't touch the game for a year (or two, I don't care). "That's not Ace Combat, that's some ♥♥♥♥♥♥ edgy-action-shooting♥♥♥♥♥♥quot; I thought to myself. But in the end I gave it a new chance and I have to admit it actually was fun. I really pumps up the action and seeing all the missile exploding, machine guns going "BRRRRRRT" and plane computer doing all weird electric noises indicating lock ons and♥♥♥♥♥♥ It was very impressive. For the first two missions. After you realise that DFM is pretty much the only useful way to destroy enemy targets (because the old fashioned way isn't really that effective) it gets really boring and feels more like chore after a while. Oh, and did I mention you that enemies can also go to DFM against you? First it seems a really nice idea, but breaking out of this DFM can be a bit hard. You need to manouver a lot and have a lighting fast reaction time to make evasive manouver when the game tells you and start dog fighting the one chasing you. Most of the time I had no idea what I was doing and just flew like a drunk giraffe and smashed buttons in hope of making succesful evasive manouver. Only time I found DFM extremely cool and well placed was the final fight with Markov, but I'll get back to that later.
As of gameplay variety there's a lot of it. You get to pilot a AH-64 Apache, be a AC-130 gunner, fly a (stealth)bomber and be a door gunner on Blackhawk. AC-130 and Blackhawk door gunner missions and just boring and bland railshooters and doesn't sit well in to the rest of the game. One thing I found funny in AC-130 mission is that they chose AC-130 because they tried not to destroy the ancient ruins. Yeah I didn't matter in the end because these ruins are made of the hardest ronk on the earth and I find it kinda funny that no one in the crew complained if you keep bombing the ruins with 120mm cannon. Wonderful.
AH-64 missions were interesting, but the control were a bit wonky. I don't know if this was because I played with contoroller but I found it to be a slight problem to adapt to helicopter controls. My advice is to not use the 3rd person view because your copter will most certainly blocks your view. Isn't that funny. In the end AH-64 missions were okay.
Bomber missions, oh my god, they really had to ruin them. Most of the bombing mission are just another version of railshooter. You HAVE to proceed in to this Airstrike Mode or ASM which forces you to move a set path and slowly move forward and bomb the♥♥♥♥♥♥out of everything. Sometimes you have only one chance and you must succesful on first try or it's back to last checkpoint. Sometimes you have option not to enter this ASM but, just like DFM, ASM is the only effective way to clear targets. If you don't enter ASM, enemy fighter will most likely come after your♥♥♥♥♥and do everything to ruin your bombing run. On B-1/B-2 mission you have no option but go to this really boring railshooter ASM. Bombing missions are big meh. Sounds cool but boring as ♥♥♥♥.
Another big complain come from the camera. Everytime you're on DFM os ASM or any♥♥♥♥♥♥mode you camera goes to most wierd angles ever and it becomes pretty hard to see. Especially on DFM the camera shakes so much it's hard to see what's going on. Also everytime something cool happens (plane exploding, structure exploding etc) the camera zooms in to the target. You can't skip and that sucks. I don't want to see everything. I want see where I'm going!
Woah, not a lot of good to say and I'm not even finished yet. Let's talk about characters. There's none. Well technically we have but they're all generic ♥♥♥♥nuggets from protagonist and antagonist to every sidecharacter. We have all these generic American heroes (including the hothead, brave leader, black guy and female member) who saves the world once again versus the evil russians with ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ general who doesn't want to cooperate with the good guys and the antagonist with tragic past and need for revenge (for some reason). No character developement whatsoever. No depth, nothing. Just boring stuff here. Just like plot. Nothing special there too.
The graphics are okay. Planes looks beatiful and the interiors are modelled too. Overall everything looks nice. Except when you lower the altitude. I understand that this is a flyinf "simulator" but if they didn't intend the ground level to be so detailed then they shouldn't have any missions/cutscenes that is seen on the ground.
Music. They really nailed it. One of the best soundtracks I've ever heard. There's good variety from dramatic orchestra to heavy metal. They final boss fight had excellent choice for music. After all the the defences have been breached, people getting panicked and all seems to falling apart, Akula appears with a pilot determined to get his revenge. Then song started and starts an intense final battle. That was truly awesome. It didn't matter how boring the plot or characters are, the music really made the moment. The music alone get's the 10/10. The sound design also ain't nothing bad. i really like sound machineguns. Hearing "BRRRRRRRRT" is really satisfying. The audio team did good job.
There's a lot of variety on aircraft. Excluding the special vehicles there's a lot of fighters to choose from and for every mission you're give a good roster of fighters to choose from. There's a lot old familiar choices and, what I saw, atleast one fictional aircraft though this was not avaible on singleplayer. Also there's different paintjobs avaible. It's up to you if you want some cool camo or shark teeths or patriotic paint or a random waifu on the wing with obnoxious color choice.
There's probably more thing to say but I think I have said enough. My summary is that even though the game lacks plot and character design the game was still fun to play. DFM brought something new to the series and was cool and fun. Also gameplay has a lot variety but unfortunately some part of the game are just boring railshooting or otherwise poorly executed. There is still a glimpse of that old familiar Ace Combat in the game but gets dumbed under the all new different mechanics. Well atleast gameplay ain't repetive. Mission are a bit long but it didn't bother me too much since you could quit the game and the resume to the last checkpoint any time you want. I think the visuals on aricraft and the music really helps the game. Still i find it hard to recommend. If you haven't played Ace Combat before then I recommend trying something else that Assault Horizon. If you have played Ace Combat before but not a fan of different gameplay, then don't get Assault Horizon. If you're truly a Ace Combat fan then go ahead, get it.

This game fun as a quick multiplayer game if both people enjoy arcade style point grabs. There are a couple endings to achieve, and that's where the problems start...
The alternate endings require you to have certain items equiped or used but the game gives very little help to figure it out. On top of all that, the important items can only be acquired by mixing which involves buying very expensive items together. I think this game would be a lot more fun if the items cost less, maybe even half their current cost. I played about 4 hours of this game to beat it and I don't really have any intrest playing another 4 to grind enough money.

This is a good game. If you've arrived at this review to see if the game is worth buying, and you have no experience with the Souls Series, then sit down and let me dispel a few myths, dispense some advice, and not spout "Git Gud" ♥♥♥♥♥♥ry at you.
Dark Souls is not hard. Hard games don't have infinite lives. Dark Souls is a fair game, and will punish you for making the same mistakes over and over.
Dying is natural. If you die, shrug, recover your souls, and carry on. Don't treat death in this game like in other games. You're expected to die in Dark Souls, its part of the game.
Do not go to the Catacombs or New Londo at the start. You will die die die die die for nothing. Go to the undead burg. Where's the Burg? When you get to Firelink Shrine, the Undead Burg is the only place you can go that goes up in elevation. Look up a map.
Use the Wiki if you get lost.
Dark Souls is a game that grows on you. At a certain point in that growth, things will become clear as to why people get addicted to this game.
And now the last bit of advice: Its perfectly fine to not like Dark Souls, Its not for everyone. My first experience with the game resulted in me getting rid of it because I just didn't have the time to learn it.

After logging about 10 hours game time, mostly just designing BOATS THAT FLIP OVER AND SINK VERY EASILY, I finally started playing the campaign.
This game seems to be the most detailed RTS concievable.  Build your units block by block if you want to.  Build your resource collecting block by block too.  Build engines and tinker how many cylinders, how many crankshaft sections, where to place carberators, more suerchargers or more local fuel tanks etc.  Listen as the torque capacity goes up and the RPMs go down!
Warning: The learning curve is rather large.  There are still non-intuitive parts of the interface.  For example, if you try to put a gun together, you might have components that aren't contributing anything just because of where they are placed, and I'm still learning to master these nuances.  Looking at a block shows whether it's connected, but it doesn't glow or somehow make it more obvious at a glance - you have to double check.
Same for engines - it's a balancing act swapping out a supercharger for a fuel tank to see if the power capacity goes up in unforseeable ways.  Maybe eventually this will all make sense (like an "aha!  that's because there was only 1 carberator there and not 2!") - but right now for me it's all very mysterious and fun.  :)
Another Warning:
The build mode also has a concept of what is being editted, which isn't clarified by the tutorials that I had gone through, so if you want to change a gun in the middle of changing the ship, I was scratching my head why it wouldn't let me place blocks for the longest time before it made sense.
I'm sure I have not fathomed everything possible in this game, but it is meting out a great feeling of satisfaction discovering all it has to offer.
--- FINAL WARNING ----
The game really does move heavily in the direction of "serious games".  These are games which try to simulate real world problems.  You can program Lua scripts in FTD, and you may want to, if you have that sort of time at your disposal.  Personally, I start to wonder if I couldn't be spending my time better programming in the real world, rather than in the game....  your mileage may vary.  :)  Chin up!
Also have a look at the very detailed models available in the workshop.  There are 1:1 ratio replicas of historical battleships and ...  lots more.

This game is a fantastic adaptation of the mechanics of Terraria (side note: I get thatg everyone compares this game to Terraria) in a space setting, and I thoroughly enjoy it. However there are some problems I have with the game, technical and preferential.
I greatly enjoy this game, don't get this wrong. But I would like to point out a few bugs that I have come across recently, as both a tip to the creators and a warning to others.
- On a fire planet - you know, where fire rains from the sky - I found an Avian village and was walking through it when some fire landed and burned off a bunch of banners from a wall, and the villagers immediately accused me of stealing them.
- Not sure if this is on purpose or not, but enemies who are targeting friendlies will not under any circumstances cease targeting those friendlies, even when I'm blasting at them with an ex machina and the other guy is running away.
- Occasionally when I destroy wild farmable plants that are immediately above caves by about a block or two, their drops will appear in the cave instead of on the surface. This also goes with other drops as well.
- In platforms within Apex science facilities, if I jump down onto a platform that is rising upward, most of the time I just fall through the platform. I assume this is because the player's code checks a certain distance below the player for a solid object to land on, but the platform gets out of the way too fast so no solid object is found.
- This one is a bit lengthy. So I am used to my own keyboard configuration where "w" is the jump key instead of space. This works fine unless I get in a mech suit in zero gravity. Usually I would set jump to "Space, W" and move up to "W" so I can use W for both actions. However in a freefloating mech suit, this does not work - when I press W, the suit does not go up. I think this is because the suit is trying to jump instead, but the suit can't jump in zero G anyway. I have had to solve this problem by getting used to using Space to jump. So far I have only died twice from this recalibration.
- This one I actually like - sometimes when you eat food, you don't consume the food item. This appears to only happen on very specific frames of the game.
- In the Hunting Grounds where the Floran relicis, one of the boulder traps sends boulders uphill instead of downhill. This is from awhile ago and may be fixed by now.
Now for a few preferential things - stuff I find slightly problematic with gameplay, and the fixing of which I would find as an improvement.
- Rain makes the game incredibly laggy at times.
- Many of the animals, especially flying ones, glitch from one place to another as if I were on a server with substantial lag. (This may actually be the case for all I know.)
- Food items such as chocolate and chili peppers are priced very high for their commonness. I have a massive plantation of chocolate from which I have created tens of thousands of pixels worth of chocolate bars in the same timespan it took to only have just found my first neonmelon. Actually, you know what, don't fix this, I kinda like it now that I think about it. Maybe we just need oculemons to be more expensive is all.
- Fine movement is difficult because if you barely tap a directional key, if you're on flat ground you barely move at all but if you're on the edge of a block you fly right off of it at a pretty high speed.
- There is a large amount of animals that attack unprovoked but a very small amount that don't attack unprovoked, and seemingly none that actually run away (besides small birds). It would be interesting to see more wildlife that you need to sneak up on.
- Learning about the existence of mech suits after completing a large portion of the game first results in a lot of progression feeling as though it has been lost, or pointless, since you need to go back to low-danger areas to farm items to upgrade mech suits when those same low-threat areas on planets are long behind being difficult for late-stage weapons. As such I think it should be made at least slightly more obvious that mech suits exist to new players, instead of simply labeling areas in space as "requires mech to deploy", since I had no idea what that meant. (I originally thought that mech was mechanical components you add to your ship; I don't watch anime so I'm not that familiar with mech suits, ok?)
Everything else I can think of is well-balanced, in my opinion. Thanks for creating and updating this game, it's really fun!
