State of Decay is a open world survival game that will please fans of the genre with its own unique ideas and a focus on character permadeath.
--------Final Thoughts at the bottom--------
The gameplay is all about survival, it really makes you feel like you want to live. This is mainly due to the fact that if the character you are playing at the time is somehow killed, then they are dead for the rest of the game. Their is no way to bring them back to life, this makes you think twice about just trying to hack your way through hordes of zombies.
Throughout the game their are moments, such as events or story missions that will pop up, about other survivors in trouble, completing these missions brings more survivors to your base. The higher your populations the more well defended you are and the more characters you have to switch out with to play. Each survivor has its owns traits and sets of skills. These skill levels can be raised by performing the activity related to the skill. For example your shooting goes up the more you use weapons, or stamina will increase the more you use the character to run around and loot with that character. However the more survivors you have at your base, the more supplies you will need to take care of them all. This means you need to go out and collect more loot.
You collect resources such as medical, building and weapon supplies, by entering abondoned buildings and searching for cuboards, draws, boxes etc.. that are highlighted white. When a supply stash is found you put it into a dufflebag and take it back to base. This however limits how much you can take at a time, if you have a vehicle you can store duffle bags in the back but if you are without a vehicle you may also radio back to base and have another runner come out to get the rest. However doing this will put that runner at risk of attack by zombies and if they run into trouble you may need to go out to save them. You may also loot various other things in buildings such as weapons, medical supplies, and food. Different weapons have different strengths and weaknesses. The weight of some weapons will also effect how some characters can swing them depending on thier strength.
The controls feel very well done and accurate, whether its swinging a weapon, shooting a gun or driving a vehicle, it all feels smooth.
The graphics are nice, I wouldn't say they are amazing or anything, although their are some breathtaking areas within the game world. The zombies look well done and their are a decent amount of models that are used so it doesnt feel like your killing the same thing over and over, however their is only one model for each special infected.
The animation is good and feels lively. Although sometimes I did feel like, for how fast my character was running I wasnt going very far distance wise. The swinging and shooting looks good and my framerate never dropped even while fighting multipul zombies and Im only on a medium spec PC.
The sound in the game is good. When out in the woods you can hear the birds and crickets around you. When in town the lumbering steps of zombies can be heard all around you. The foot steps sound realistic for the type of platform your character is on at the time. Guns sound good and hitting zombies with melee weapons sounds satisfying.
The voice over work is good, nothing fabulous or game changing, but its good. Their are multipul different characters taht are all voiced however some of them sound like they were voiced by the same person and didnt even try to sound different.
Thier is not much to say story wise. There is a story that will eventually lead you out of the city and end the game. However the story plot is basic and it seems like it was just shoved in their to appease some people who want to complete it, but it is not neccesary.
Overall, State of Decay is a great game that is definetly worth the time for anyone whos a fan of survival or zombie games. It is a large world to explore and loot with many different survivors to save and add to your community. The game has some fresh ideas from other zombie survival games, and these ideas are portrayed very well. The visuals are nice and the animation is good. The permadeath may set some people off from this game, also if you are looking for a story, this may not be the game for you.
In my opinion this is one of my favourite PC games and is fully worth the full price, however be aware that their is a remastered HD version coming out soon so you may want to hold onto your money for that one. (EDIT: After the release of the remastered version I would still recommend this version over the newer one. The new one just spruced the visuals up a bit but change very little in terms of gameplay. If you want to save some money, just get this version.)

Fast paced, brutally difficult, and beautiful 2D arcade shooter. You play as a customizeable superweapon and lay waste to clouds of fighter planes, massive battleships and submarines, and more.
Pros
- Tight control scheme with very enjoyable ship physics. You can easily pick up the game and play with little experience, and you will also learn fancy maneuvers over time and get better at dodging the clouds of bullets and missles that await you.
- Great ship customization, switching ship weapon, chassis, and engines. 125 possible ships (and one secret ship).
- Nice 2-D art, with fantastic animations. In addition to the sepia classic color scheme are a range of unlockable color palettes which cause varying amounts of eye-bleed.
- Cool chiptune soundtrack. Your choice of ship parts will change elements of the soundtrack.
- Nice missions system for every ship part. Completing missions unlock other ship parts, ship backgrounds, and the punishing difficulty mode SFMT.
- I have personally never experienced any glitches or performance issues. HOWEVER: When you collide with another ship, gametime runs a little more slowly, and you might think the game is running choppily when this happens.
Neutral
- Extremely difficult gameplay, especially in the SFMT mode. Game quickly becomes a bullet hell, with quite low ship health and only one life per run. You will die a lot. You might like that.
- Two difficulty modes, normal (quite difficult) and SFMT (virtually impossible). SFMT is difficult enough that you get an achievement for surviving 13 seconds.
- Purely arcade game modes, no story or multiplayer to speak of. It's all focused on the gameplay, so if you don't dig the 2D dogfighting there's nothing here for you.
- Some aspects of the game are very RNG based. You can get missions to kill specific enemy types that appear some small percentage of the time.
Cons
- Two of the achievements are obnoxiously difficult to complete, compared to the others. You will complete every achievement except the last two by 15 hours of gameplay. You might want to contact a mental health representative before attempting to complete all achievements in this game.
- Visual style can make it difficult to understand exactly how damaged you are. You will often think you can eat a bullet that ends up killing you.
- While the chiptune soundtrack can be customized a bit by your decision of ship parts, it has the exact same structure and mostly sounds the same between different combinations. It can be tedious, but you can always mute it and play your own music when you get tired of it.
OVERALL: For me, this is an excellent arcade game. Great controls, exciting difficult gameplay, and a really fun aesthetic. All of my cons, besides the first one, are pretty small gripes, and for me the neutral points are mostly positive. I highly recommend the game.

This might be fine for someone who just wants an air combat game to play, but if you're a fan of the older AC titles like AC04 this just isn't for you.
Several major elements have been changed for jets: Your machine guns never run out of ammo, and neither do your missiles, they simply have a cooldown period. There's also a new "chase" mechanic which locks you onto an enemy and autopilots you around, making aiming your only concern in a dogfight. It's basically rail shooter mode. Not only is this boring and unchallenging, but it also looks ridiculous as you weave between buildings and oil rigs at mach two. Use of this mechanic is optional against most enemies, but certain VIP targets force you to use it in order to take them down.
The helicopter missions come in two flavors: awkwardly controlled attack helo and boring rail shooter transport helo. There are also gunship rail shooter missions straight out of CoD.
Overall everything feels very scripted like a CoD game and there isn't a lot of room for stages to play out differently when you replay them. There's no tension because you never run out of ammo, and there's no challenge because of the autopiloting chase system.
If you're a long-time AC fan like me you'll probably hate this game. If you still buy CoD games then this is for you.

A true masterpiece. I've been gaming for close to thirty years and Dark Souls is among the best games I have played. I didn't know a thing about it until I stumbled into it on Steam after having beaten Mad Max. The latter I still think is a very good game, but Dark Souls is on another level. There is no hand-holding, no map--you are alone in this haunting, strange world wherein early enemies who look laughably frail will own your nooby a s s. I very quickly realized how bad I had become at open world action games. I remember being so bad and cowardly, afraid of enemies, terrified of the Taurus Demon, and petrified at the thought of being invaded. It makes me laugh now. Eventually you'll git gud.
Unfortunately, it's a bad port with garbage multiplayer connectivity; however, both of these failures have been fully erased by great modders whose mods you can easily download and get up and running quickly. Even the 720p 30fps can be modded away very easily. The game looks gorgeous at 1080p and runs at 60fps with very few issues. The community is alive and passionate about the game and the forums have all the answers. I play most of my games vanilla so if I can get mods running properly, anyone can.
If you want a challenging environment and the added difficulty of having other players invade your world to slow your progress, Dark Souls is the game for you. This game is special. You will remember your first time playing through it; you will remember entire areas of the game; you will probably want to play it through again many times with different builds or with your character at NG+ and beyond.
Don't fear the difficulty. Don't fear the invasions. Don't take PVP personally. With humility and patience you will persevere.

I have to say this is one weird game. Keep in mind this opinion comes from a total noob in regards to flight simulator genre,
, and any games with planes in it. The first time I "seriously" play a flight game was
on Xbox 360, and I ended up cockpit first into a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ ground texture. So yeah, I suck at this kind of games.
Things that kind of stick out to me is how the game having "look over there!"-cutscenes. I don't know about the other
s, but having told what to do/see via a cutscene always annoys me. You have UI, target designators, stay with it! There are also non-mandatory ones, triggered by a button press when it comes on screen, which I guess you could ignore but I always pressed it anyway.
And you also get treated with ocassional slow motion scenes when you destroy a target. I honestly doesn't find it to be a bad thing (and make for a nice footage, if you're into video editing) but it does break the flow of the combat, somewhat.
But the mechanics that actually feels like, "they're kinda watering down the genre, aren't they" is the DFM, or Dogfight Mode, system. Basically when you are locked on on an enemy, you can activate some sort of an "automatic enemy chasing" mode. All you have to worry about is maintaning speed so your enemy doesn't get out of range or being to close to them and being countered by their own DFM (which obviously make that enemy auto-chase your plane.)
Although relying too much on DFM could be fatal since limited maneuver means you can't dodge incoming misilles, as the loading screen usually tell you.
It's not exactly a bad system, but it does make the flight techniques less... elaborate, for a lack of a better word, especially since the game itself made the use of the system to be mandatory at times. At one point, I even had to restart a very short segment of the game for at least five times because I was out of the DFM too soon and getting a Mission Failed screen, even if the target is already
. You could also argue that the helicopter missions also break the game, but I found it to be an alright distraction from all the plane crashes.
All in all, I don't really recommend this game for big fans of flight genres. It feels too "arcade-y" and the gimmick system could prove to be an annoyance at times. Unless you don't care about any of that and just want to do some dogfights. Or doing dogfights with (or against) friends. Or you're just
desperate to see more of the 765 idols in video games. Like me.

edit: I'd rather be a neutral review but a proper party really makes all the difference for.. all (boss) fights.
Port seems okay for the most part. Still has some problems. 60fps seems to have downsides so I switched to 30fps to avoid it all. The purple fungus fight can SPIN TO WIN on you making it impossible with 60fps on and you can not outrun it. You might be able to avoid it, but I doubt it. I didn't know until I looked at the forums on how to fight the impossible.
Normal may be less annoying, but I have it set on Hard.
Boss fights lean to very annoying minigames with a few that actually involve combat fighting (at least two so far). Pinball (King Shishkebaboo) was very annoying but I think it may be a mix of my citizens failing to reach the rock at several times when I send them and.. something. Small things like that build up that make the game much more frustrating than enjoyable (and pinball is a physics minigame that I got tired of. It would have been a bit 'easier' if I had more miners and more HP since I did eventually get the rock down in seconds in one of the attempts)
The Long Sauvage was a mix of frustration but doable after a while. Using the 'wrong' formation doesn't allow you to hide in the mine shaft doors. Even the right formation sometimes doesn't hide your Little King completely and you can peek out and take damage. A few times I lost my entire party because I wasn't hidden entirely and eventually slowed down to make sure everyone was.
The game crashes randomly sometimes. A few times on a map and a few times when I was in a boss fight. Might be able to force it to crash calling citizens using the podium. Sometimes the .exe doesn't completely close and you have to force quit it as well.
The battle system gets a bit tiring when you face an enemy that can instantly kill your party. Send out your troops for 0.5 seconds, retreat, repeat. Hope for a stun effect so you can actually deal damage. You can use the ranged troops to prevent that game, but you'll run out of arrows unless you go back to the castle often or use a full party of them.
The game itself is probably better looked for opinions elsewhere. I'm enjoying it for the most part, but the minigame boss battles aren't what I would call enjoyable (except TV DInnah unless you don't pay attention and mindlessly play) and I will probably suffer for the last 2 or 3 once again.

Ooh, where do I get started with this game?
Ultra Street Fighter IV was released as a "expansion" to SF4AE and SFxT, balancing the game where it was needed (Bison, Seth, Cammy and Fei Long, I'm looking at you). In that sense, USF4 accomplished what it was meant to do, be the perfect SF4 experience and deliver a fighting game based on Street Fighter 2.
Do I recommend it? Yes, but thats not the only thing about the game there is to be pointed out.
USF4 can be extremely dumb. Even though its skillcap is far higher than SFV, for instance, compared to other fighting games, its quite low. The game to a higher level of competitivity is intersting, but many characters, even in the Pro Scenario, are still incredibly stupid, hence the game being based on Street Fighter 2. Wanna know exactly what Im talking about? Check USF4's finals from 2015. Momochi basically won by spamming Hadoukens and 2 easy punishes in the last round that was deciding the finals.
USF4 is not a bad game, at all. I actually played this for quite a while in PS3 before playing it on Steam. Its a fun game, hard to learn and quite technical in comparison to nearly every game. But as a player that came from 3rd Strike, I will never agree with someone that says that SF4 is the best Street Fighter game or that SF2 is the best Street Fighter game. SF4 is a really good game of the fighting game genre, perfect for fans of the genre, but not all that great in comparison to other fighting games one could play.
As for games that are better than USF4, there are many. And I do mean, many. From the Street Fighter series, there's 3rd Strike, imo the best fighting game ever released, Alpha 3 and 2nd Impact. The MvC series is full of infinites and a completely different gameplay, but the skill gap is far higher. In the SNK side, even if I barely played SNK games, KOF 2002 and Garou require far more skill, knowledge and technique to play then USF4.
USF4 is the typical 3/5.
tl;dr: If you like fighting games, play it, you'll have a fun time. If you TRULY like fighting games, there are better games out there. If you don't like games that need actual skill, dont even bother.

Shadow of Mordor is a game that I don't think gets enough praise for what it offers. On the surface, this game looks like every other Assassins Creed clone out there. You hop over roof tops, assassinate people from above, do lots of sneak missions and so on. I agree that this is a great way to sum up the general style of the game.
However, there are lots of little things that make this much more enjoyable to play. For a start, the combat is considerably better with a combo style you'd find in Batman Arkham Asylum. Each sword slash is quick, straight to the point and delightfully violent. On top of this, you also get some very nice magical abilities that are also very fun to use. The stealth and bow attacks are just as smooth and easy to use. In fact, this is the best stealth from this type of game that I have played. This is due to the character being quick, very responsive and generally stress free.
This is all down to the fact that the controls have been very well implemented. The character moves at a reasonably fast pace at all times that make even the slowest parts of the gameplay quite quick. The wall climbing is not as rigid as Assassins Creed etc and very fast. There is also a lot more surfaces to climb on compared to these games. This means you can move about on all terrains very smoothly, making this a considerably more enjoyable experience.
The story itself is not bad by any means. It has absolutely no relevance to the book or the films and kind of makes up its own lore which is a shame. It also doesn't utilise any of the amazing music from Howard Shore, that is also a bit of a let down since the music is fairly generic. The characters are reasonably likeable for the most part, but it would have been much nicer to have them a little more faithful to the lore.
Considering how often this game is on sale, I would highly recommend it. Much like the underrated Mad Max game, It is generally very well made and was quite fun to play for the 15hrs I was in it. It definitely deserves a bit more praise for what it does well, even if it has some glitches here and there.

Review for waste walkers.
Just to recap the game for those who have never heard of this game;  its basically taking the idea of fallout with the nuclear war, and turning it into a proper RPG that has a turn based battle mechanic instead of it being a FPS.  The game itself is set after the bombs that have landed, and brings a unique vision on the "Post apocolitic wasteland".
There's a few things I would quickly like to mention; even tho this had the concept of fallout written on it, it is still a completely different game wish much hours of enjoyment to be had, there's seveal mechanics that RPG players will appreuate.
Mechanics; Level based Stats, Learn able skills, Compaions, Crafting, Looting, bartering, turn based battling, character customisation and a large amount of quests.
Each of these could be a lenghty explenation why I personally like them, but i'll keep it short but sweet.
Level based stats;  This is good especially for this game as it does get progressivly hard the more you level up, and the stats actually count for something (they are explained at the beginning of the game)
Learnable skills;  This gives the feel of acomplishment when you finally do learn a useful new skill, these can honestly be the diference between life and death.
Companions; We all love having some sort of assistance with people aiding us when we need it, but this also helps with the inventory system to.
Crafting: You're able to craft few items but this can obviously be improved.
Looting: This is basically a way of life within the game loot->sell->use->repeat.
Bartering/traiding; this allows to keep yourself stocked up in weapons/armour and stuff to survive the harsh wold waste walkers is set in.
turn based battling; a very nostaligic thing for me as I love turn based games, it brings a aspect from years ago that is lost amoung current games...unfortunetly this will still be a thing in the past.
character customisation:  Theres not much in this aspect but you can chose your; name, stats, skills and cosmetic skin.
I would happily rate this game 9/10 for the fact it bring a lot of nostaligia to it, would recommend getting this game!
Also been talking to the dev a little; Some interesting stuff coming soon.
Did i forget it has "hardcore mode"? Basically get water and food to survive ;)

This is a very impressive and very different rpg from Corrosive Studios that can and will entangle you in its story, its atmosphere, its high quality, and its intricate detail from the very start.
Your main character at the beginning is starting to leave a farmhouse (where he has taken shelter from a nuclear disaster) in an effort to find his family. But what he finds is a world of radiated monstrosities, unforgiving and relentless bandits, curious survivors, and next to nothing to eat or drink. And so the danger filled journey of survival and discovery begins.
At first glance, you will see the usual mechanics and workings of the old school rpgs, but you will quickly realize that there are a host of different parameters that have to be carefully, and wisely, monitored in order to have success in the game. And that is a huge positive ---- it makes you think carefully about every move you make, every building you enter, every battle you find yourself in, every supply you are offered to pick up and perhaps use, and every choice you make involving other characters you meet along your journey.
You have to watch not only your HP, but your stamina, your hunger level, your hydration level, your radiation level, and other factors that will be important to your success or failure.
Fortunately, there are several save slots so the "trial and error" method can be used ---- at least, for me.
It is simply a game that will make you think about your very next move all the time rather than just fighting and leveling up to get through. Selecting the proper strategy is paramount ---- and that is a big aspect that makes this game so much fun to play. The challenge is high, but fair ---- with a lot of "Why didn't I think of that before?" moments.
Additionally, the mechanics and controls of the game are easy to learn, and work flawlessly.
And the sound effects, along with spooky music, yield a creepiness factor that is a huge plus to what's going on. You easily get into the atmosphere of the story in no time at all.
The game is constantly being updated and added to by a dev that obviously cares very much about perfecting the game experience and offering us something different that stands out.
Well, right now I'm stuck in a bank with feral dogs snapping at my heels, so it's back to it for me ---- and I would urge anyone to give this tremendously entertaining and highly polished game a chance. It is well worth the time at an excellent price. Highly recommended.

Painful and rewarding. These are the words that describe Waste Walkers.
Combat is mostly meant to be avoided, as these enemies are not mass production mooks.  Each and every enemy has their own perks and abilities, but most importantly, they are fighting to survive, just like you are. Carefully avoiding enemies while you loot containers is a sensible idea, and completeing quests is more effective for gaining exp. Enemies do currently scale with the player and his comrades, but this never feels overly annoying.
Crafting is simple, as are most quests. Simple does not mean easy, as many of these items are in the hands of dangerous individuals or randomly generated. The rewards are subtle, but they will benefit you either in spare cash and exp, or in better services and cheaper supplies. They can even gain you access to powerful and vital supplies. Crafting can help make your life cheaper and easier, once you buy the scematics. Crafting may be limited to what you can make, but they can save you much time, effort and resources if you are determined enough.
It is not to say there are no flaws, but that is mostly due to resource limitations. WW is a large game for an opening title, and is still rather fun.
Overall, Waste Walkers is a survivors fight for his life, and an enjoyable experience for those who likewasteland exploration games.

I simply cannot stress enough how amazing of a game this is. Hands down, it's up there with the best gaming experiences I've ever had. I finished my first playthrough after 80 hours, and I must say, I'm looking forward to future playthroughs greatly. This is a game that truly emphasizes what importance the use of exploration, planning, strategy, and not rushing can do for your overall experience. It's not just a game that you can power through, run-and-done, and if the player chooses to do so, they're missing out on a bunch of amazing content. So, for those of you who are looking to grab this game (it goes on sale quite frequently), behold my review of DS1, and all it has to offer. (No spoilers! :D)
So, where do I even start? Well, I guess the first thing that comes to mind is the world and environment itself. Dark Souls has no spoon-fed story that's easily recognizable and given to the player. The story is communicated through extensive lore, whether it be through item descriptions, the way NPC's talk to you, the environment, or even just the enemies' appearances and attacks. If you truly take the time to analyze what's going on around you, you begin to understand more about the mysterious yet clue-filled land you're immersed in. It's very satisfying, wondering about where or why something is the way it is, and over time piecing together the clues to figure it out. And what makes it so fun, is that the overall lore and story can be subjective. You may find some pieces of evidence that lead you to believe a certain claim, whilst another person may have found different evidence that leads them to believe the opposite. It's all about how you interpret the game, and it’s huge hidden story.
The game's physical playing field is also very expansive and is intertwined throughout itself throughout the entire game. The level design is completely unparalleled to any other game I've played before and is very unique. You'll find yourself spending a few hours running around from area to area, only to find out that there was a secret shortcut hidden in an alcove leading back to the main area. Or maybe you've just stumbled across a narrow bridge that leads to treasure, only accessible through the visibility of a light. These little things, while not very big, begin to add up. They promote exploration and thought. And they create a world so immersive and connected, that it's almost hard to believe that people had to plan all of this stuff out!
Moving on to the combat, it's something that's never really been seen in other games; maybe with the exception of Dark Soul's predecessor, “Demon's Souls". Dark Souls combat is different. And it's really, really good. People will say "OMG DARK SOULS IS SO HARD WTF HE JUST KILLED ME IN 5 SECONDS!!!". And yes, it's challenging, but it's completely fair. 95% of the time you die, it's your fault. You can't just rush in and expect to hack and slash everything because chances are you're going to get ganked by all sorts of different enemies and overpowered. You have to use your logic. You have to take your time in battle, plan out how you're going to take on a situation, and take advantage of different scenarios to pop in a heal or maybe switch your weapons and gear. It's not a risk/reward sort of system, and if you treat it as so, you're often going to be dead much more often than you are actually playing. Notice how the different enemies use attacks, or maybe, how your own weapon's moveset works. Take time to recognize your situation. And use the lessons you've learned in previous encounters as your strengths in the next.
Bosses are very interesting because most of them are these gigantic, intimidating figures that are very powerful. But, believe it or not, they're not too hard to defeat, especially if you know how. This is a FromSoft game, and if there's one thing I know it's that there is pretty much not a single enemy or boss that you can't take advantage of in some way, whether it's simply using their elemental weaknesses to your advantage, or full-on cheesing the hell out of them by brutally annihilating them before you even enter their line of sight. In any case, the combat is very well polished and makes you really pay attention to what is going on, else you may suffer the consequences of the "YOU DIED" splattered on your monitor.
So hopefully at this point, I've given you a glimpse into what this game is like. But there's so much more beneath the surface, and given that this game goes on sale for 50%-75% off on Steam regularly, it's a no-brainer to pick it up just to try. And remember kids, Praise the Sun!

After previously holding off, because of the various warnings about its performance, I bought the game when the 02-02-17 patch was released. One thing I noticed was that the king sometimes keeps moving forward after I have let go of my left analog stick. My controller is getting older, so it is very much possible that is not caused by the game.
The graphics are an upgrade from a game that was released a couple of generations ago, so they are not going to blow you away. Still, the cartoony look does not really require the most advanced graphics anyway, so as long as the game looks nice and crisp and runs properly, I'm more than fine with it. The art style of the game -- just look at the king -- does shine through though and this elevates the graphics quite a lot.
The game itself is really fun to play and I can see why so many people are praising it. For a more in-depth analysis, I would suggest checking the other reviewers, since they are way more knowledgeable and I have yet to finish it. I mainly wrote this review to inform others that were anxious about the performance issues. I would suggest to make the purchase when there is a discount, because the price is a bit high even if the game is worth it.

This game is truly a gem. If you like/d Pikmin, this game is very similar while also being unique enough that it doesn't feel like a clone. Made by the creator of Harvest Moon, it's a pseudo-city builder slash adventure RTS game in which you control a young King. Your goal is to expand your Kingdom and take over the world by throwing your subjects (literally) at monsters, in order to clear the area so you can expand there.
The graphics are very childish and cartoon-y, but definitely not unpleasant. For almost a decade old game, it looks nice, even on low settings.
There's a surprising amount of fun to be had in the game, and it's difficult to tear yourself away once you've gotten into the groove of throwing and exploring. It's also shockingly challenging at some parts and requires a good deal of thinking for some boss battles.
Story: 7/10
The story is admittedly rather simple, but the dialogue is funny and there's lots of humor and parody.
Graphics: 8/10
With the upgraded gfx options, the game looks great. The artistic direction is fantastic and very endearing.
Gameplay: 8/10
The core gameplay is great. My only issue is with the pointer controls - for reference, I'm using an Xbox 360 controller. You can use the left trigger to target specific enemies, but even then, often times your people will go flying in the wrong direction. It's really annoying, but not a deal breaker imo; you just need to be careful with your aim. Otherwise, the gameplay is very fun and has a hidden amount of depth in terms of classes and strategy.
Audio: 10/10
The music in this game is great and suits the art style perfectly. Seriously, this game has a wonderful OST.
Overall: 8/10
If you like Pikmin and similar RTS games, and don't mind the cartoonish graphics, I highly recommend  Little King's Story, especially with the upgraded port.

-No in-game map (dev tells me this will be fixed eventually)

I may include a brief review at the very end of my ramblings so for those of you looking for a quick and easy nudge in the proper direction you can easily see what I was discussing.
Anyways, I shall not digress any further; to begin the mechanics I stumbled across in this game captivated me to a extent of what was there to work with. With the game still currently in beta I can understand there are elements still needing to be refined and with the short playtime I have on record thus far which at the time of the review is only about four hours at most. I find a appealing factor in Waste Walkers, one of which is brought upon the enjoyments I find out of other games such as Fallout which no doubt is the game's premise centered around. The system has a while to go until it is fully layered to the point where replayability can be found. Some of the quests (Such as one involving a couple in the department store) could do with more plot development other than a guilt tripped woman going about her life in a monotonous pattern. You could argue that these strangers bare no important role in the big picture and that I would agree upon; however with quests that are straight forward. Quests that seem to be daunting with simplistic tasks and not having a overall drive of actuality behind them (Remember only four hours in) I could find how some would become very bored with the game rapidly.
However, I have given the game a shot and I believe in my own opinion it has aspects of which are desired. Aspects of which to grow and expand, lessons to step forward with and to become its own community of wastelanders. I truly believe that for a start up beta, what is offered currently is enough to drive itself further and further. IF Corrosive Studios is capable of pushing their work of art in the proper direction and building a game not just merely a clone of what Fallout is, but a unique blend of what a survival rpg is. Bringing in their own sense to the terminology of what it means to be throw to the barrens of the wastes and how you must survive in a dog eat dog world. For this genre is riddled with video games that just don't chalk up to what they desire to be and with the first steps Waste Walkers has taken and the aspects of its survival, the managment of resources, the exploration of a expanding world and the ability to not only live a story through a character but to write your own story in it of itself is appealing to be in the helm of. There could be more strategy involved, not only in the combat but in the tactics a player decides to do; how to achieve a goal and what the player is destined to do to obtain said goal in their own terms which would make it more survivalist in the end.
This game will only go as far as the developers wish to take it, and if a community were to form around it then I would happily become engrossed with it. I hope the review I left to whomever may read it gave you a tidbit of what Waste Walkers has to offer and as of writing it I may have been critical and focused on a topic of questing systems but for a game to jump into I believe it is worth a shot.

Ok so here it is my incite into the relentless iradiated rollercoaster of a ride that is Waste Walkers!.
Do not for one second let the cuddly pokemon style graphics and gameplay that this game is made like because that is as far as it goes!. You will be bitten,stung,chopped,bashed,poisoned,iradiated and much more on your journey through the wastes!. You wil encounter insects,ghouls,bandits feral dogs and more that are not a push over so you better avoid them untill you are well prepared and equiped and even then beware it is about survival not combat so be warned ! ;p
If you are a Fallout fan then you are going to love Waste Walkers in the way that takes ths style of game back to it's roots, even if you have never played Fallout and are not familiar with the franchise you will love Waste Walkers ,it is a fresh take  on the relentless world of nuclear apocalypse with all of the worlds end wonder we have come to know and love!.
It is very fluid to play especially if you are familiar with pokemon style rpg which is how the gameplay and control system are similar too except you will die a lot.... oh yes you will die many times whilst you learn to play due to the fact it really is a survival game unlike many that claim to be this will make you work hard to truely survive.
The loot systme is epic many many buildings etc to loot all with randomly generated loot tables, a very good rpg level up system and char creation with skills and techiques some of which are passive, a great crafting system with schematics to craft various items ,weapons,armour meds etc also there is a hunger and thirst mechanic of which you will need to find food and drink on your travels through the wastes.There is also a geiger counter which sounds when you are being iradiated, i have only played 4.9  hours so far so there is much more i have not discovered as well as new content to come.
All in all it is an exellent title showing what a solo independent developer can acheive ,he is also keen to take on board suggestions and communicates with the community very well indeed and at 19 years old has put many other indy early access dev teams to shame, i wish Corrosion well and hope he goes on to be very sucessful ,the game industry thrives on people like this that go on to be what makes gaming epic!.

Luftrausers isn't an especially complex game. It's simple, but in the same way, say, Gradius or Pac-Man is simple. It's incredibly easy to play, it's fast and frantic to play even with the slowest combination of parts, and it only takes a press of a button to start it up once again. The premise even somewhat resembles the basic stories you'd see on arcade shooters; you're a lone pilot taking on what appears to be the British military over an endless expanse of sea, swapping out various guns, bodies and engines to make your killing machine. Speaking of which, the parts system is very well-designed, with each piece feeling unique and changing up the playstyle completely between runs. Beyond this, little needs to be said about Luftrausers. You launch your ship, you shoot opponents down, and you get points. It's a simple and pure arcade-style shooter, and that's what makes it so good.
Is Luftrausers hard? Yes, often ridiculously so. But it's so insanely fun that you can't help but give it one more go, pushing your top score as high as you can, fighting larger and tougher enemies and cutting it incredibly close in the process.

"This is a story about an undead struggling against the world. And this is the story of a player struggling against Dark Souls." It's all connected. Everything about the game is designed towards achieving a certain goal, and that's what makes it special.

I simply cannot stress enough how amazing of a game this is. Hands down, it's up there with the best gaming experiences I've ever had. I finished my first playthrough after 80 hours, and I must say, I'm looking forward to future playthroughs greatly. This is a game that truly emphasizes what importance the use of exploration, planning, strategy, and not rushing can do for your overall experience. It's not just a game that you can power through, run-and-done, and if the player chooses to do so, they're missing out on a bunch of amazing content. So, for those of you who are looking to grab this game (it goes on sale quite frequently), behold my review of DS1, and all it has to offer. (No spoilers! :D)
So, where do I even start? Well, I guess the first thing that comes to mind is the world and environment itself. Dark Souls has no spoon-fed story that's easily recognizable and given to the player. The story is communicated through extensive lore, whether it be through item descriptions, the way NPC's talk to you, the environment, or even just the enemies' appearances and attacks. If you truly take the time to analyze what's going on around you, you begin to understand more about the mysterious yet clue-filled land you're immersed in. It's very satisfying, wondering about where or why something is the way it is, and over time piecing together the clues to figure it out. And what makes it so fun, is that the overall lore and story can be subjective. You may find some pieces of evidence that lead you to believe a certain claim, whilst another person may have found different evidence that leads them to believe the opposite. It's all about how you interpret the game, and it’s huge hidden story.
The game's physical playing field is also very expansive and is intertwined throughout itself throughout the entire game. The level design is completely unparalleled to any other game I've played before and is very unique. You'll find yourself spending a few hours running around from area to area, only to find out that there was a secret shortcut hidden in an alcove leading back to the main area. Or maybe you've just stumbled across a narrow bridge that leads to treasure, only accessible through the visibility of a light. These little things, while not very big, begin to add up. They promote exploration and thought. And they create a world so immersive and connected, that it's almost hard to believe that people had to plan all of this stuff out!
Moving on to the combat, it's something that's never really been seen in other games; maybe with the exception of Dark Soul's predecessor, “Demon's Souls". Dark Souls combat is different. And it's really, really good. People will say "OMG DARK SOULS IS SO HARD WTF HE JUST KILLED ME IN 5 SECONDS!!!". And yes, it's challenging, but it's completely fair. 95% of the time you die, it's your fault. You can't just rush in and expect to hack and slash everything because chances are you're going to get ganked by all sorts of different enemies and overpowered. You have to use your logic. You have to take your time in battle, plan out how you're going to take on a situation, and take advantage of different scenarios to pop in a heal or maybe switch your weapons and gear. It's not a risk/reward sort of system, and if you treat it as so, you're often going to be dead much more often than you are actually playing. Notice how the different enemies use attacks, or maybe, how your own weapon's moveset works. Take time to recognize your situation. And use the lessons you've learned in previous encounters as your strengths in the next.
Bosses are very interesting because most of them are these gigantic, intimidating figures that are very powerful. But, believe it or not, they're not too hard to defeat, especially if you know how. This is a FromSoft game, and if there's one thing I know it's that there is pretty much not a single enemy or boss that you can't take advantage of in some way, whether it's simply using their elemental weaknesses to your advantage, or full-on cheesing the hell out of them by brutally annihilating them before you even enter their line of sight. In any case, the combat is very well polished and makes you really pay attention to what is going on, else you may suffer the consequences of the "YOU DIED" splattered on your monitor.
So hopefully at this point, I've given you a glimpse into what this game is like. But there's so much more beneath the surface, and given that this game goes on sale for 50%-75% off on Steam regularly, it's a no-brainer to pick it up just to try. And remember kids, Praise the Sun!

Your reaction to this game, be it positive or negative, will likely mirror your reaction to the following sentence:
If you just want a quick review, that's probably all you need to know.
If, for whatever reason, you would like me to
elaborate, I will do so.
First, it is necessary for me to admit here and now that as a longtime fan of the Ace Combat series, I personally, am unable to give a truly unbiased review of this game. As such, my issue with this entry in the series is primarily the drastic departure from the core gameplay of said series. There are a multitude of these "departures", many of which you've likely already heard complaints about, and thus I won't go into. Now if upon reading this your assumption is "This person is just bitter that they changed the gameplay around", I wouldn't hold it against you, as you'd be right.
To be fair, there is a lot of good in this game. The presentation is great. Everything looks good, and this game has probably the best visual detail we've seen in this series so far. The sound is excellent as well, ranging from punchy and immersive (if not always realistic) sound effects, to the little things, like the multilingual onboard computers of the various planes, not to mention a fantastic soundtrack.
One may ask, "Who then, is this game geared towards?" Well, to put it bluntly, this is a game for casuals. I'll spare you the old jaded gamer diatribe, and say this; If you simply want a flashy casual action game, then this game was deliberatly developed and marketed towards such a demographic. It even says so on the cases of physical copies of the game; "Call of Duty in the air", and that's exactly what it is. That, in and of itself, is not bad. That said, this game, being what it is means I must repeat this sentiment:
Why then, are these contentious issues? Well, quite frankly, Ace Combat is a niche series. This game could quite easily have been presented as a spinoff with a different title, which may or may not have alleviated some of the negative reaction, who knows. Thing is, this game carries the Ace Combat name for brand value. A brand that, in all honesty is not as popular or widespread as my fellow fans and I, and perhaps Namco-Bandai as well, would like to believe.
Having said all of that, it seems as though the developers have realized this, as the game that followed this title; Ace Combat Infinity (PS3 exclusive as of this writing) has gone back to the "old" style, though not without its own share of issues, which I won't waste even more of your time with. So perhaps this game was, in a way, a necessary step. By that, I mean, in regards to seeing what would work and what wouldn't. In the end, did it work? Well, that depends on your personal viewpoint on this statement, which i'll repeat for the last time:
When all is said and done, this is not a game for us, the Ace Combat fanbase. But what about you? Maybe you don't consider yourself a "hardcore" fan. There's nothing wrong with that. And if that is indeed the case, you might just enjoy this game.

I really wanted to like this game.  Platformers and ARPGs are my absolute favorite types of games to play, and I'm interested in most things with a fantasy, paranormal, or medieval aspect.
This game seemed to include fantasy, platforming, and alternate/parallel realities that you can switch between. I thought it would compare to Chronology, Giana Sisters Twisted Dreams, and Contrast.
Unfortunately, I found myself frustrated with the poor controller function. I'm not an impatient gamer, so I hung with it awhile, but no matter how hard I tried, there was no consistency to the controls. Sometimes controller function worked the way I expected, and sometimes it didn't. In games like this, though, there must be consistency. You can't have "quick-switch" mechanics if the controls are unreliable.
For example, in an early level where you see the text, "sometimes just wait," I couldn't move to the right or left and jump at the same time, and just simply jumping didn't get the character where it needed to go. I finally gave up and just fell off the first landing to the left, only to land at the finish line below. That shouldn't happen.
The graphics and artwork were okay and even a bit interesting from a minimalist standpoint, but I did notice the poor grammar in some of the text.
This game needs a lot of work, but I'd be among the first to pick it back up once changes are made.

A rather simple game where your stats affect your daily life as a princess. Beginning of the week you choose your classes to study in order to increase your stats and your mood affects your progress of each class.
The objective of the game is to survive 52 weeks until your coronation, while your decisions definitely have an effect on whether if you will be exposed to danger, your stats will determine whether if you survive the various ways you could be killed.
You can choose to resolve disputes/ problems in multiple ways and the higher you are with the relevant stat the more options open up (eg. high Military - Strategy stat will allow you to select an option to go straight into war instead of parley)
Having played it for a little amount of time I am loving the various options and consequences of my actions and it definitely has a high replay value
The only con I have found in this game is that the ending is somewhat the same no matter how you survive.
Nonetheless I would recommend this to anyone who wants a challenge of the mind or simply a game where you feel like your choices matter.

Do NOT be fooled thinking this is a princess simulator trying to get handsome men to marry you. The game is dark and depressing, and it's good... REALLY good. Everything is out to kill you, and most of the time, only you and your decision can save your life. This is a quick pros and cons I'm gonna do since I'm in class and won't be able to pull a full review:
+Well written plot and character interaction that can immerse you.
+Everything is out to kill you. The game is completely unpredictable.
+ You can be a loli hitler or a magical girl or a swordmaster queen. Whatever works!
+ Be a scum: Create scandal, assassinate people, lie your way through!
+ Be the ultimate pacifist: Deus Ex Human Revolution no killing playthrough too easy for you? Try surviving this game without killing anyone!
+A LOT of attributes to level up ranging from riding a horse, archery, internal affairs, controlling your anger, casting fireball, how to dress up... Damn, just about everything.
+Be as stupid as "Hospital? Why would you want to put sick people together? They'll die faster!" to as smart as managing your not-so-big but vicious little army to conquer the world!
+SO MUCH MORE
- The game is difficult. No seriously, try to get a decent ending without dying at least three times. It's to the point where you will think the game is cheaping you out, but that makes completing it even more fun!
-The art could use some work.
-Music can get tediously repetitive sometimes.
-Unpredictability seems unfair sometimes. (The wizard battle *cough*)
-Surprisingly short if you know the game inside out.
Overall, this game left me with a huge smile on my face when I finished it.

If you just look at it for what it is, a Beta, I think it's fairly well-designed and the developers are actively invested in what their playerbase wants. I'd love to make some deep-fried Seagul cooked in rendered boar fat and ground yucca flower breading but I don't see even differentiating between white and red meats anytime soon.
If you really like the survival aspect of games like Day Z or The Forest, but generally don't care for the combat, I'd say invest in this beta. I've gone through several dozen playthroughs all at various degrees of completion, but I'm still finding myself playing it every now and again.

This game, for an early access game, is marvelous. This is the first game that I have ever reviewed, steam or not, and am only reviewing it because of the negativity I have been seeing about it.  This game is everything you should want from a survival game.  It has a huge open world that you can craft, loot, and pvp against other players and it is not just a spray and pray game.  You have to actually be good at strategy and aiming in order to do well in this game.
There are also people complaining about the updates that the developers make in this game.  I see no need to complain about the devs making updates that mainly focus on literally fixing the game that they wish to be able to take out of early access.  I am fine with being their guinea pig for as long as they need.  They should take their time and push out a good product and not be like ark who insisted on getting out of early access even though their game was still riddled with bugs, and it still is, and they still ignore it, and still just make content updates.  Miscreated has a content update once a month or if they dont have a content update in one month, its a bug update, and then the next one is a content update.  Give them some credit for expanding a map that literally takes hours upon hours to fully explore and traverse already.
Sure, the developers have made mistakes but they are not a huge team like these other big games.  One of the things that people ask for most from the developers is more storage space and they have stated time and time again why they do not want to add in more and I do not blame them for getting a bit sassy with saying that there are other games out there suited to what you want to play.  I agree with that statement made by them, this game is literally survival, you should not be able to store a thousand guns and ammo in your base by simply going outside and chopping down 20 logs and making a ton of crates.  That isnt survival, that is just easy.  They are way better than just making another "ark clone" as everyone else likes to throw around when any new survival game pops up.  This game is absolutely wonderful and well worth the $20.00.

Ultra SF4 is the best Street Fighter game Capcom has released in the last 10 years. Given more time, I'd say it may even be better than my beloved SF3: 3rd Strike. What's great about Ultra SF4? Additional characters from Street Fighter x Tekken (Poison, Rolento, Elena, Hugo, etc) plus a brand new character (Decapre). Speaking of SFxT, they even ported over some of the Capcom-themed stages from that game.
New to Ultra SF4 is now the ability to enable "Edition Select" - so you can play as practically any version of the character you selected (ie. Vanilla SF4, Super SF4, Arcade Edition, etc.) as well as this brand new variant called Omega mode! Omega versions of each character has brand new moves and quirks. Capcom really did a good job of making each Omega version of the characters completely different. Gameplay wise, a "red focus attack" is now added - this enables your character to absorb multiple hits for greater damage at the cost of more stocks of Super guage meter.
Overall, this is a terrific fighting game for veterans and beginners alike. Much, much better than SF5, in my opinion.

An awesome game that stays true to the spirit of the series, with brutal battles, and an onslaught of enemies that you could very easily die to, especially in the early game.  The nemesis system, being the shining star of the title tells a story that allows you to create the future for your playthrough.  The main story, however, is uninspired to say the least.  The sidequests with Torvin are easily the best part, as the rest of the characters are about as unremarkable as they come.  With stunning gameplay and battles, superb graphics, and at times frusteratingly difficult captains (Looking at you, Knosh the Brain Damaged.  Being immune to literally every attack is  pretty well a guaruntee to become my Nemesis) the game still culminates into a fever pitch when you storm the black hand... only to be greeted with quicktime events instead of an actual final boss fight.  Extremely lazy, and ultimately underwhelming.  The biggest flaw in what is an otherwise superb game.
In all, is the game perfect?  No.  Far from it.
Is the game worth the price I paid on the humble bundle?  Definitely.

Guilty gear Xrd was, and is, a revolutionary fighting game - not to mention a new take on the medium of videogames and fighting games as a genre.
At the time of this writing, the game's largely obsoleted by Revelator. While the original plan was to have just a single 'Xrd' game, with new content added as DLC updates, meddling on the part of Valve ('a contract is a contract is a contract!'), as well as Arc being new to the whole thing, that didn't came to be, and Xrd is essentially a graveyard.
However, one must remember it for what it was, is, and aimed to be, not what ended up as. Rather than the 'traditional' formula of essentially zero singleplayer content, heroic scale characters, karate men with karate uniforms doing karate sumo wrestling on each other from 1992 to 2015, little to no continuity, and an unwillingness to challenge established norms, Xrd returns to what made the series so great and successful, and refuses outright to deviate from the, and I quote, red path. No corners were cut, no challenge considered too great, deadlines were met, and no expenses spared - which considering the small team and minimal budget, is quite the accomplishment.
If you don't know, and odds are you might not, GG has and always will be masterminded by Daisuke Ishiwatari, a man who has a very clear, very defined vision. When other franchises go wild with singleplayer modes, he and his handpicked teammates read between the lines. It's not singleplayer that's in vogue. It's an entire experience. So Xrd features an extensive three act anime movie, that while not comparable in technical prowess to what would come in Revelator, features an all-star cast, and ties up ten years of questions, while also weaving in formerly very unpopular/poorly received features, like guilty gear 2 overture's story changes.
Everything, the anime movie included, has an 80s style to it. 80s guitars, characters with lines that would have fit in just fine in fist of the north star, plot twists that seem absurd at first glance, but make more than enough sense when examined even cursory, not to mention designs that go above and beyond the self-parody that is modern day final fantasy. For instance, Sol Badguy has a grand total of 34 zippers and belts, which is more than your average FF character, but he carries himself with a purpose and flair that makes him less about the belts and zippers, and more about his 80s brit-scene metal theme songs, his gameplay flow, and the voice acting. In short, the whole package.
In a sudden return to form, Ky, formerly perfectionist child soldier and warrior prodigy, is allowed to grow as a character, while also returning certain essential characteristics that haven't been seen since #Reloaded and the accompanying books and drama CDs. Hint. he's a devout christian, and has had a lifelong struggle with the fact that all he's ever been good at, all he's ever had in life, and all he's ever been noted for, is how incredibly, utterly, incomprehensively masterful he is at killing everything and everyone, but to mark that he's actually for real grown, rather than the traditional, casual call out that he's setting up for a finisher ('sacred order ultimate forbidden technique. RISING FORCE!') he recites his oaths to his family and kingdom in a most biblical fashion, no calling the move necessary, charges full speed through a master level lightning magic circle, to remind us of why this regular human dude is able to hang with bio-weapons, monsters, the undead, and other assorted weirdos, gives a most humiliating, but for once actually true, one liner, puts on his cape, and just walks away matter of factly. I believe it's up there in the top ten most boss moments of videogames.
Speaking of the voice actors, you'll be hard pressed to find a franchise with a more star studded cast, and like the gameplay and attention to detail, it's never waivered, and never will. It's hard to believe it's been almost two decades since Takeshi Kusao starred in the first ever guilty gear on the playstation, and in a sense, he's largely typecast himself as Ky. A fun little thing is watching the future Trunks episodes on dragon ball super. He tries very hard to do Trunks, but in the end, they give him a lighting sword, sacred edges, and lets him do the equivalent of a rising force destroy on the big bad, and it's hard to disbelief his conviction.
So would I recommend a fighting game that's essentially got no future due to executive meddling? For 15 dollars or less...surprisingly, yes. There's enough singleplayer stuff here for at least 20 hours of fun, and I consider Xrd an essential purchase for anyone who considers themselves a guilty gear fan. While a lot of mocking has been thrown at the animemes, the production value makes it worth your while, and just getting the universe explained to you, especially if you maybe played an X2 game in the long distant past, is pretty useful. Also note that while Rev is the future, Rev as far as we know will never feature the Xrd singleplayer stuff, mostly importantly the story mode. Another important thing to note is that Arc, unlike about 99.99% of all other publishers, absolutely love and cherish their fans and community, and will give you price cuts on future games in a franchise if own old entries.
Future updates will be added to GG Revelator. When you're reading this, odds are, that game is on Rev 2.
As a side note, it's incredibly interesting to me that 80s animation tricks and voice actors that actually knows what they're doing manage to outshine, outperform, and completely obliterate modern day anime, even when the anime is merely a fanservice addition to a fighting game, and the fighting game in question is on unreal 3 of all engines.

I came to this game and immediately found it interesting.  Very similar to RPGs of the past, this game relies on map navigation and battles take you to a separate screen where you fight in turn-based combat style.  After a number of hours playing, though, I found the game frustrating and extremely confusing.  Fortunately, I was able to get a hold of the developer who seemed to genuinely care about my input into the game.  The game itself has great potential and, while it is an unfinished product, is continually being updated.  If you want to decide whether to get this game, here are some of the pro's and cons:
Pro's--the exploration is fun and there is a lot of exploring to do in the game.  Fog-of-war makes for intense travel, though this option is toggleable.  The game is constantly being updated and the owner seems to be making an extra effort to change the game and listen to his customer's input, while at the same time continuing on the theme and direction of his game that he's had.  There is a crafting system in the game and many interesting locations to discover, as well as some basic quests you can find to do for good rewards.  The music is nice and creepy, which is aesthetically pleasing for those who like the 'zombie' feel to a game (though there are no zombies in this one!--too bad :().  There are a host of weapons, armor, and items to find and use to give you an advantage over the many enemies out there that will most likely tear you a new hole if you aren't careful (especially at the beginning).
Con's--while the game has great potential and is improving everyday, it still has it's flaws--and some of them major.  Because it is an RPG-based game, anyone who seeks these elements may be disappointed with the level progression for stat-based characters.  I've played a dex-based character and an endurance-based character and I can honestly say--dex seems nearly meaningless (and even this he has changed a bit recently, so I can't say if this is still ongoing).  If you go all-out endurance and gain access to respectable armor, fighting enemies will be cakewalk, even ones 1-2 levels above you.  If you choose any other statistic to focus on, you'll get♥♥♥♥♥♥♥  And not just a little bit.  Like--2-3 round♥♥♥♥♥♥before you die.  The stats I would say are currently extremely unbalanced.  The other major issues I have is, the game completely lacks a glossary of terms and a manual to give even the noob basic pertinent information to survive in his/her adventure.  While they have a 10 page intro, that information should be readily accessible at any given time (because most noobies forget stuff like this).  But even so, the 10 page tutorial doesn't cover many of the frequent abbreviations and/or terms you might be wondering (what the hell does this do?)  Also, there is no functional map.  They have schematics for maps, but none of them work.  Because of how this game is built--its not like a square by square dungeon with easy navigational mapping--I think it's absolutely essential to have a map for this game.  There should be, if nothing else, an offline map we can access--but to my knowledge there isn't even this.  The last thing I found very irritating is the MP bar (and don't confuse this with magic points, as I did and ended up dying a number of times till I realized it wasn't magic!).  In every RPG I have ever played, MP refers to magic points, it is just below the HP bar, and it is the color blue.  Well, their 'moral' bar fits all of these bills, as well as having the abbreviation MP on the status screens...but it's not magic points >_<.  I think the developer will change this, but for any noobie playing this, I can guarantee you would have confused this for magic points unless you read my review.  In addition, pretty much most places you go in to the game and loot--it's all the same stuff.  You're looting meds, food, and drink.  There is the occasional place that has housed some guns (which I've found much later on), but these places are so few and far between it makes little difference.
With this said, the game is improving and has great potential.  The owner went out of his way (even spending hours with me offering tips--though not all were good ones--and I was delighted to see that he cared and took the ones he felt would improve his game and has/will implement them.  While I cannot currently offer a thumbs up for this, the game has great potential and I'll be continuing to keep my eye on this game.  It won't be long before this will be a force to recon with other games on the market of a similar nature, like the traditional fallout games and dead frontier online.

Okay so before I review I would like to tell everyone or anyone who plans on buying Waste Walkers that this is a Early Access and that it will of course have bugs and glitches..So without further ado! Here is my review of this game called Waste Walkers.
This game is very unique and you start out inside a basement of a house (That might be yours.) and you scavenge for resources that you can use to survive, but before that you can customize your character which is something I find pretty neat!
Your objective is to survive but that's not the only objective..You can choose to help people that need assistance such as getting an item for them.
While i have only came across one glitch it is a really great game so far! The bug or glitch i came across is when you go to the police station and you grab the key to the armory..When I grabbed the key and opened the door it still would not let me through..But that did not ruin the experience for me in anyway..I kinda was happy that it happen because then it would make everything way easier.
Why do I recommend Waste Walkers? Because it is unique and I have yet to see a Survival RPG Maker game on steam..And a game such as this is amazing as it is well done, the developer is new in game designing and needs support. I am willing to lend him my support seeing how he did a great job on this game! Sure I have only had 2 hours in the game..But in those 2 hours, It was a fun experience and I know there might not be much in the game..But i know this game is worth supporting or paying $6.99 for..To be honest i don't think it should be $6.99..But maybe the price will change when it is a full game.
The next thing I like about the game is the hydration and Food meter..Now you have to eat alot in order to heal yourself..Sometimes I eat food so i can heal but sometimes i eat it when I am low on hunger or hyrdration..Regardless I think the food meter and hydration meter is a cool thing because it adds more survival into it..Oh! And did i mention there is a Radiation meter? Well there is! And if you get near vehicles the meter will go up.
Now..I know this is weird and kinda stupid to like..But how the levels of monsters or bandits in Waste Walkers..What i find cool about it is that when you level up, so do the monsters and bandits..Which is pretty impressive because I know that when you are making maps or layers I know it isn't as easy as you think.
Finally here are my thoughts or ideas on what i think should be put in Waste Walkers and if you are reading this developer I hope you continue to soar high and continue to make unique games. You have my support!
Here are ideas or my thoughts on what should be in the game in the future:
Relationship System/Love System - Even when the world ends, People still find love or fight by each other's side.
Pets -You can tame or befriend wild creatures and such.
Storyline - While this may be a game focused on surivival..I would like to see a storyline.
Adoption - In a post-apocalyspe world there are those who no longer have parents..I would love to see a adoption feature so when you saw a child that is outside or whatever by himself/herself then you could choose to adopt him or her.
A Night/day system - While it may be nighttime in Waste Walkers all the time..I would love to see a night time/day time feature as it would be cool and make it more realistic even though it is a RPG Maker game.
Supernatural NPCS or Characters - I would love to see supernatural beings such as Succubus, Demons, or any other mythological supernatural character or beast..But not just any Supernatural Character or beast..But characters that could imply to the relationship system up top..For an example: The character could be walking down the hallway and he or she thought he or she heard someone behind him or herself..But when he or she turn back nothing was there but when he or she looked back the succubus or demons appeared before him or herself.) The relationship/love system would be the same as the other NPCS or characters..But the supernatural characters or mythical creatures could be completely different because of how they talk or act.
A bigger world - Exactly as it is titled..This idea would be that you could do some missions or quests and have them completed in order to acquire the item that can lead you to another city, town, area, or world.
House/Fort System - I would love to see this in this type of game because you could litterally be at home but you can get raided and such..Which I think would be pretty cool!
Family system - I think it would be cool to see this espically if you had the house/fort system since you could have certain characters control or maintain certain things.
And that is all for my review! I hope this helped anyone who was heistate to buy this game!
EDIT: Also when I say that it shouldn't be $6.99 I did not mean that in a bad way. It should be higher then $6.99 but that is just my opinion.

If you want a realistic flight simulator, skip this game and go look somewhere else. This game is about pure action and does not bother with realism the slightest.
If you don't mind carrying 200 missiles in your fighter jet, shooting down fleets of enemy aircraft, and dodging missiles by making barrel rolls with your helicopter, as long as the adreline rush is there - then this is the game for you.
Ace Combat: AH will not impress you with its story and its many seen-from-miles-away plot twists. It will however keep you in the heart of the action from the beginning till the end; it is very good at keeping the tension up all the time, making you feel like you're in a constant rush - and you will be. You're the guy defusing the bomb with its timer nearing zero, except you're doing so in an aircraft, and there's a new bomb every 5 minutes.
While the difficulty curve is erratic at best (some missions are very easy, while some can get frustrating - especially the last one which sees a huge spike in difficulty and can result in many a scream at the screen), the adreline rush is there all the time - whether you're engaged in a dogfight with another fighter jet and trying to match its movements as it zig zags between buildings in the heart of a city, whether you're saturing the sky with missiles to keep enemy jets out of the hair of the transport you're defending, whether you're dropping dozens of bombs on an enemy base to blow it up while dodging incoming SAMs, whether you're sending salves after salves of rockets from your Apache helicopter at incoming columns of armour to prevent them from reaching your too-vulnerable infantry, or whether you're trying to out- or counter-manoeuver an enemy jet who's tailing you, your breath will be held from the beginning till the end of the fight. That's the real strength of this game.
So if you want an fast-paced, action-packed aerial shooter with a much appreciable soundtrack which complements its intensity in a very fitting way, go ahead and give this game a try. It's not the longest one of the bunch nor the most mind-blowing, but it'll keep you entertained for its 10~ hours worth of material, and will offer you more if you want to keep at it.
The battles can be kind of drag on, and seem like forever. But, it's a pretty sweet game all around.

Do not take notice of the 1 hour playtime, I have worked my xbox to death playing this game. This review will focus on the gamplay and mechanics, story is not as important for this game. Lets start the review!
When State of Decay first appeared on my Xbox 360 dashboard I thought of it as another cheap Zombie arcade game, I decided to download the demo and since that day, I have been hooked. This game throws you in the midst of zombie apocolypse and lets you know your only option to survive is to group up with other characters. You then go through the game saving (or leaving) survivors and inducting them into your community which you build up, choose what to build, where to build and what base will be yours.
This game takes realism to the extreme, all characters that you can switch between have their own personalities that effect how they react in situations and how their mood is during their stay in your community. They also have their own skills, weaknesses and backstories that let you know what person you want over others and let you feel a connection with these characters. With so many different personalities staying under one roof in such a severe time, problems are bound to happen and sometimes you may need to help calm down a survivor or go take them out and have a chat, maybe someone is scared or upset and needs you to give them reassurance that everything will be alright and this level of realism for what actually would happen in this situation is amazing.
One thing you must keep track of is supplies, having a large community may keep it safe from zombies but starvation and illness can hurt large groups. You will need to scavange and set runners to go collect these resources to reimburse the daily supply usage.
The best thing about this game is the death, in State of Decay if somone dies, they die. Runners going to get supplies and get caught up by a horde? dead. Survivor is ill and there is no supplies? Dead AND infecting others. This really gives the incentive to stay aware of whats going on and doing your best to keep everyone alive, I let my guard down when I got near the end of the game and ended up with the games first character dead because I left him alone when he needed help. There is nothing more sad than having to go collect your dead friends bag.
This game is a must have for any survival lover, 10/10!

I really wanted to like this game.  Platformers and ARPGs are my absolute favorite types of games to play, and I'm interested in most things with a fantasy, paranormal, or medieval aspect.
This game seemed to include fantasy, platforming, and alternate/parallel realities that you can switch between. I thought it would compare to Chronology, Giana Sisters Twisted Dreams, and Contrast.
Unfortunately, I found myself frustrated with the poor controller function. I'm not an impatient gamer, so I hung with it awhile, but no matter how hard I tried, there was no consistency to the controls. Sometimes controller function worked the way I expected, and sometimes it didn't. In games like this, though, there must be consistency. You can't have "quick-switch" mechanics if the controls are unreliable.
For example, in an early level where you see the text, "sometimes just wait," I couldn't move to the right or left and jump at the same time, and just simply jumping didn't get the character where it needed to go. I finally gave up and just fell off the first landing to the left, only to land at the finish line below. That shouldn't happen.
The graphics and artwork were okay and even a bit interesting from a minimalist standpoint, but I did notice the poor grammar in some of the text.
This game needs a lot of work, but I'd be among the first to pick it back up once changes are made.
